children.text: tatrādāv eva nirvighnaṃ prārabdhakāryasiddhyartham abhīṣṭadevatānamaskāram āha ||
children.translated_text: There, at the very beginning, for the unobstructed success of the work that has been undertaken, he states the salutation to the desired deity.

children.text: iha rasakarmāṇi caturaśītiḥ guṭikābhedāścaturaśītiḥ añjanāni caturaśītiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the alchemical operations are eighty-four; the varieties of pills are eighty-four; and the collyria are eighty-four.

children.text: evaṃ te dvipañcāśadadhike dve śate bhedāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus those varieties amount to two hundred and fifty-two.

children.text: tata eteṣāṃ bhedānāṃ madhyād yadaikā kācit kriyā prārabhyate tadā prārambhātpūrvaṃ māsamekaṃ brahmacaryarūpaṃ tapaḥ kartavyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, from among these varieties, when any one operation is begun, before the beginning one should perform a month of austerity in the form of celibate discipline.
For celibate discipline itself is the root of all austerity.
And because every other austerity, when deprived of that, is fruitless.
Or, celibate discipline should be maintained.
And likewise austerity should be performed by the teacher and others according to what is appropriate.
For both are the first root of the fruits of all rites.

children.text: tathā haviṣyānnaṃ ghṛtaśarkarāmiśraṃ pāyasaṃ kṣīrabhojanaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, one should take sacrificial food, rice pudding mixed with ghee and sugar, and milk-food.
For with other foods there is no purification of the body.
And because there is no accomplishment of prāṇāyāma.

children.text: tata evaṃ karma pālayatā tatkarmaphalaṃ yāvan netavyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, observing the rite in this way, one should carry that rite through until its fruit is obtained.

children.text: yato rasādikā kriyāḥ sādhake bhraṣṭe yathoktabhojanam akurvati na sidhyanti ||
children.translated_text: For alchemical operations concerning <s>rasa</s> and the like do not succeed when the practitioner has fallen away and does not take the prescribed food.
Nor do they bear fruit when the austerity has been lost.
And he himself will make this clear at the end of the treatise.
The disciple's statement is: "I shall teach the chapter received from the presence of the venerable yogin <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>."
In that chapter the linked <s>rasa</s> has been set forth by reasoned procedures such as herbal steeping, fire-heating in sealed crucibles, and the like.

children.text: yathā kila śṛṅkhalā pūrvapūrvatarāvayavair anyonyānupraveśāt sambaddhā bhavati tathā atrāpi ||
children.translated_text: Just as a chain is connected because each earlier and still earlier link enters into another, so too here.
First comes the purification of <s>rasa</s>.
Then comes the revivification and raising up of the purified <s>rasa</s>.
Then the distillation of what has been revived and raised up.
And again the raising up of what has been distilled.
Then the steaming of what has been distilled and raised up.
And through steaming, the brought-under-control state of what has been steamed.
The obstructive or restraining power of what has been brought under control.
And the straightening out of what has been restrained.
And the digestion of mica in what has been straightened out.
And the digestion of metals in that in which mica has been digested.
And the digestion of ayas-prakāśa-rāji in that in which metal has been digested.
And the digestion of hema-rāji in that in which ayas-prakāśa-rāji has been digested.
The digestion of sulphur in that in which hema-rāji has been digested.
And the digestion of the essence of realgar in that in which sulphur has been digested.
And the digestion of the essence of khāpara in that in which the essence of realgar has been digested.
And the digestion of annapatha-diamond in that in which the essence of khāpara has been digested.
And the binding of that in which diamond has been digested.
The flowing or projection of what has been bound.
And the killing or calcination of what has been projected.
And the penetration of that which has been killed.
And the binding of what has penetrated.
And the opening up of what has been bound.
Thus.

children.text: evaṃ pūrvapūrvatarasaṃskārasya rasasyāgretanasaṃskāro granthito'stīty asau procyata iti tattvam ||
children.translated_text: In this way the later refinement of <s>rasa</s> is linked with each earlier refinement, and therefore it is called that; this is the meaning.
The twelve defects of <s>sūta</s>, that is, mercury,

children.text: teṣāṃ doṣāṇām apagamopāyaiḥ śuddhiṃ nirmalatāṃ tato'ṣṭādaśa pāṭasāraṇādīn saṃskārān pūrvaṃ vadāmi ||
children.translated_text: and, through the means for removing those defects, purification, that is, stainlessness; then, first, I shall explain the eighteen saṃskāras such as pāṭasāraṇa.
After that, the fruit of the perfected <s>rasa</s>s, consisting in the production of silver and the like.
Then the production of gold, rājya and the like, and of essences such as khāpara.
Then that which accomplishes the body,
and the <s>rasāyana</s> that accomplishes metals: this I shall explain. Such is the statement of the disciple of the venerable <s>Kaṅkālaya</s>.
Here he states the answer to what was promised, in order.
All three verses are clear.
Only, there are two each born from tin and lead.

children.text: iti dvau vaṅgajau doṣau dvau ca nāgajau ||
children.translated_text: Thus there are two defects born from tin and two born from lead.
<s>Kapālī</s> and <s>kālikā</s> are the fourth and fifth.

children.text: vaṅgajau doṣau śyāmakapālikā ceti ṣaṣṭhasaptamau nāgajau eteṣāṃ caturṇāṃ lakṣaṇamāha ||
children.translated_text: The defects born from tin are called śyāmā and kapālikā, and the sixth and seventh are born from lead. He states the characteristics of these four.

children.text: dugdhe kvathite sati yādṛśī tarā upari bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When milk has been boiled, the sort of skin that forms on top,
a similar one on <s>rasa</s> is the tin-born defect.
And the lead-born kapālikā appears on top.

children.text: śyāmā ṣaṣṭo doṣaḥ pañcavarṇo bhavati kālikā ca pañcamo doṣaḥ kṛṣṇavarṇa iti ||
children.translated_text: Śyāmā, the sixth defect, has five colors, while kālikā, the fifth defect, is black in color.
Now he states the five defects of <s>rasa</s>.
The verse and a half is clear.

children.text: atra ca jalamadhye mṛttikāpāṣāṇajalāntarasaṃyogāt tathā dugdhopari tarāvac ca ye dṛśyante te kañcukā ucyante ||
children.translated_text: Here, those things seen in water through contact with clay, stone, and water, and also like the skin on top of milk, are called sheaths.

children.text: ye punaḥ kodraveṣu madavadbhavanti te doṣā iti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But those which occur in kodrava grain like intoxication are the defects; this is the distinction.
Now he states the disorders of these defects individually.

children.text: aṣṭāpi ślokāḥ spaṣṭā eva kevalaṃ cilharī kuṣṭhabheda eva ||
children.translated_text: All eight verses are clear; only, cilharī is precisely a variety of leprosy.
Thus ends the account of the defects and qualities of <s>sūta</s>.
The group of five verses is clear.
These are the eighteen saṃskāras of <s>sūta</s>.
Now, explaining the saṃskāras in order, he says:

children.text: prathamaṃ sūtaḥ ślakṣṇavastreṇa gālanīyo yathā vaṅganāgajāḥ pūrvoktavikārāḥ sarve vastre lagitvā tiṣṭhanti ||
children.translated_text: First, <s>sūta</s> should be filtered through a smooth cloth, so that all the previously mentioned disorders born from tin and lead stick to the cloth and remain there.
Thus the first saṃskāra is pāṭasāraṇa, filtration through cloth.

children.text: ekaṃ palaṃ suniṣpannaśvetaloṣṭajīkakasya catuḥṣaṣṭipalāni ca pāradasyobhayaṃ saṃmelya khalve kṣiptvā praharamekaṃ mardayet ||
children.translated_text: One pala of well-prepared white loṣṭajīkaka and sixty-four palas of mercury should be combined, placed together in a mortar, and ground for one prahara.

children.text: yathā kālikāṃ tyaktvā nirmalībhavati pāradaḥ iti mardanasaṃskāro dvitīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As mercury becomes spotless after giving up its blackness, so this is the second process, the processing by rubbing.

children.text: snuhīdugdhena khalve rasaḥ kṣiptvā sapta dināni mṛdyate ||
children.translated_text: Mercury is placed in a mortar with the milk of <s>snuhī</s> and rubbed for seven days.
Then the earth-born coating departs.

children.text: evaṃ sapta dināni arkadugdhena mardite pāṣāṇakañcuko yāti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, when it is rubbed for seven days with the milk of <s>arka</s>, the stone-like coating departs.

children.text: palāśasya parpaṭān jalena kledayitvā tato vartayitvā vastreṇa niścotya raso grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The bark-flakes of <s>palāśa</s> should be moistened with water; then, after rolling them and squeezing them out with a cloth, the juice is to be collected.

children.text: tena rasena sapta dināni raso mṛdyate ||
children.translated_text: With that juice the mercury is rubbed for seven days.
Thus the water-born coating departs.
The two and a half verses are clear.

children.text: kevalaṃ vajraḥ snuhikandaś ca śūraṇas tayo rasena ||
children.translated_text: Only the vajra and the tuber of <s>snuhī</s>, and <s>śūraṇa</s>, are to be used with their juice.
Or else the tuber called vajra grows in mountain soil.

children.text: sarve'pi kañcukā yathoktarasena saptadināni sūtamardanena naśyantīti ||
children.translated_text: All the coatings, then, are destroyed by rubbing the mercury for seven days with the juices stated above.
And here this is the traditional instruction.
In the mortar, over the mercury, the juice of the medicines mentioned above is poured.

children.text: yathā yathā sūto bruḍati tathā tathā mardanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As the mercury sinks down, so it should be rubbed again and again.

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair yadi cāgretanauṣadharasaḥ śuṣyati tadā punaḥ kṣepaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If the medicinal juice in front gradually dries up, then it should be poured in again.

children.text: evaṃ saptadināni yadi marditaḥ pārado bhavati tadā kāñjikena kharalo bhriyate punaḥ śanairmṛdyate tato vastravartayaḥ kṣiptvā tathā mucyante tathā vartiprāntāḥ bhūmau laganti ||
children.translated_text: When mercury has thus been rubbed for seven days, the mortar is filled with sour gruel, and it is again rubbed gently; then cloth wicks are put in, and they are arranged so that the tips of the wicks touch the ground.
Through them the sour gruel filters and passes away.

children.text: evaṃ sūtaḥ sarvair apyauṣadhaiḥ saptadināni piṣṭvā paścāt kāñjikena kṣālyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way mercury, after being ground for seven days with each of all the medicines, should afterwards be washed with sour gruel.
And these eleven medicines are as follows.
Milk of vajra.
Milk of <s>arka</s>.
The bark-flake of <s>palāśa</s>.
A decoction of <s>citraka</s>.
The vajra tuber.
<s>Kaṭutumbā</s>.
<s>Bīaṅka</s>.
A decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
Again, a decoction of <s>citraka</s>.
<s>Aśvagandhā</s>.
<s>Nāhi</s>.
<s>Aṅkudhya</s>.

children.text: atra citrakakvātho dvivelaṃ vidyate 'to dvādaśabhir auṣadhair ekādaśaiva iti sūtaśodhanasaṃskāras tṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here the decoction of <s>citraka</s> occurs twice; therefore, though there are twelve medicines, they are really only eleven. This is the third process, the purification process of mercury.

children.text: pūrvarītyā śodhitaḥ pāradaḥ khalve prathamaṃ trikaṭukvāthena pūrvavat saptadināni sampiṣya śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Mercury purified by the previous method should first be ground in a mortar with a decoction of the three pungents, as before, for seven days, and then dried.
After that it should be washed with sour gruel.
In the same way, with the juice of <s>bhūmidūdhelī</s>, then with the juice of fresh ginger.
After that, with the juice of <s>karmāīra</s>.
Afterwards, with the juice of <s>devadālī</s>.

children.text: sapta sapta dināni mṛditvā śoṣayitvā kāñjikena dhāvanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After being rubbed for seven days with each, dried, and washed with sour gruel.

children.text: evaṃ ca kṛte 'sau mūrchitotthitaḥ pārada ityucyate tejasvī ca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, that mercury is called revived from swooning, and it also becomes brilliant.
Thus ends the fourth process, the raising of what has swooned.
Now, according to another opinion, the raising.

children.text: mūrchitotthitapāradasya sarvottamatāmracūrṇasya dvātriṃśattame bhāge lavaṇaṃ ityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For mercury that has been revived from swooning, salt is to be one thirty-second part of the finest copper powder; this is the meaning.

children.text: sarvasarve ekīkṛtya nimbukarasena saṃmṛdya mṛkṣaṇopamā pīṭhī kāryā ||
children.translated_text: Combining absolutely everything, one should rub it thoroughly with lemon juice and make a paste resembling an ointment.
Here this is the traditional instruction.

children.text: yāvanmātro rasastasya caturthe bhāge tāmracūrṇaṃ dvātriṃśattamabhāge lavaṇam ||
children.translated_text: For whatever measure of mercury there is, copper powder is one fourth of it, and salt is one thirty-second part.

children.text: nimbukarasaś ca tathā kṣepyo yathā sarvamauṣadhaṃ majjati ||
children.translated_text: And lemon juice should be added so that all the medicine is submerged.

children.text: adhike doṣo nahi hīne tu doṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If there is too much there is no fault, but if there is too little there is a fault.
Whenever it dries, it should be added again.

children.text: mardanaṃ ca tāvad yāvan mṛkṣaṇopamā pīṭhī ||
children.translated_text: The rubbing should continue until there is a paste like ointment.

children.text: ghaṭārdhasadṛśe kaṭāhe'dho mṛttikāyāḥ kuṇḍalī kāryate tac ca kaṭāhabundham ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: In a pan resembling half a pot, a ring of clay is made below; this is called the bottom of the pan.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvakṛtāṃ tāṃ pīṭhīṃ tatra kaṭāhabundhe kṣiptvopari ācchādanārthaṃ sabalacikkaṇavastrasampuṭaṃ tāḍayitvā tasya vastrasya prāntān kuṇḍalīṃ paritaś cikkaṇamṛdā tathā limpedyathā jaṭitā iva te bhaveyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the previously prepared paste is placed there in that pan-bottom; over it, for covering, a packet of strong, smooth cloth is struck down, and the edges of that cloth all around the ring are smeared with smooth clay so that they become as if matted together.

children.text: tatastaṃ kaṭāhaṃ jalārdhapūrṇasthālikāmukhopari pradhvaraṃ muktvā sthālīkaṇṭhakaṭāhabundhakasaṃyogasthāne karpaṭamṛdaṃ dṛḍhaṃ dattvā kaṭāhamadhye chāṇakāni ghaṭīcatuṣkaṃ yāvaj jvālyante ||
children.translated_text: Then that pan is placed inverted over the mouth of a bowl half-filled with water; at the joint between the neck of the bowl and the pan-bottom, cloth and clay are firmly applied, and cow-dung cakes are burned in the middle of the pan for four ghaṭīs.
Then, by the heat of the fire, the mercury passes out through the openings in the threads of the cloth and goes down into the water situated in the bowl below.
The copper, however, remains stuck right on the bottom.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi pūrvavat tāmracūrṇapāradapīṭhīṃ kṛtvā kaṭāhabundhasajalasthālikāyantreṇa pūrvavadraso jale pātyate ||
children.translated_text: Then once again, as before, a paste of copper powder and mercury is made, and by means of the apparatus consisting of the pan-bottom and the water-filled bowl, the mercury is made to fall into the water as before.

children.text: evaṃ saptavāraṃ rasapātane kṛte kuṇṭhatvajaḍatvādayaḥ sūkṣmadoṣā yānti ||
children.translated_text: When the falling of the mercury has been performed seven times in this way, subtle faults such as dullness and inertness depart.
This is the fifth process, the distillation process of mercury that has been raised from swooning.

children.text: pūrvasmin yoge pātanasaṃskārārthaṃ tāmrātsūtaḥ sūtāc ca tāmraṃ pṛthak saptavārakṛtam ||
children.translated_text: In the previous recipe, for the distillation process, mercury was separated from copper and copper from mercury seven times.

children.text: ihāpi yoge tadeva kariṣyate paraṃ tatra pātanāyehaiva pātitasyotthāpanāyeti viśeṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this recipe too the very same thing will be done; but the distinction is that there it was for distillation, while here it is for raising what has been distilled.
And that is as follows.

children.text: rasapala66 tāmracūrṇapala16 lavaṇapala2 sarvaṃ nimbukarase mṛditvā pūrvavatpīṭhīṃ kṛtvā sthālikāyāṃ kṣiptvopari ca madhye mukhasthālīṃ dattvā dvayormukhayoge karpaṭamṛttikayā lipyate ||
children.translated_text: Sixty-six palas of mercury, sixteen palas of copper powder, and two palas of salt are all rubbed in lemon juice; after making a paste as before, it is put into a bowl, and above, in the middle, a mouth-bowl is placed; at the junction of the two mouths it is smeared with cloth and clay.

children.text: eṣa ḍamarukanāmā vidyādharanāmā ca yantra ucyate ||
children.translated_text: This is called the apparatus named <s>ḍamaruka</s> and also named <s>vidyādhara</s>.

children.text: tato yā upari sthālī tasyā bundhe bāhyapārśve gomayaṃ dattvādhastanasthabundhādho yāmamātraṃ mṛduvahnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after applying cow dung to the outer side of the bundha of the upper pot, a gentle fire should be kindled below the lower bundha for the duration of one yāma.
Then the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) flies up and goes into the pot situated above.
And the copper remains in the lower pot.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ saptavāraṃ sūtotthāpane kṛte raso vyāpako bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When the raising of the <s>sūta</s> has thus been done again and again seven times, the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes penetrating.
"Penetrating" means sharp and possessing the nature of spreading.
Thus ends the sixth saṃskāra, the raising of the fallen mercury.

children.text: śigrunāmno vṛkṣasya pattrāṇi gāḍhaṃ mṛkṣaṇopamānāni vartayitvā teṣāṃ piṇḍena kulhaḍīṃ kṛtvā tasyāṃ kulhaḍikāyāṃ pūrvavidhinā tāmraṃ parityajyodgīnaṃ rasaṃ tathā dvātriṃśattamena bhāgena lavaṇaṃ ca kṣiptvā tāṃ kulhaḍīṃ vastre baddhvā tadvastraṃ davarakeṇa kāṣṭhe baddhvā tatkāṣṭhaṃ sthālyāḥ kaṇṭhe kaṃcana paṭṭaṃ baddhvā sthālīmadhye tribhāganimbukarasasahitakāñjikaṃ kṣiptvā kāñjikopari ñūbamānā tathā vastraṃ baddhvā kulhaḍī moktavyā yathā kāñjikaṃ na lagati kevalaṃ bāṣpo lagati ||
children.translated_text: Taking the leaves of the tree called <s>śigru</s>, making them into something like a dense rubbing paste, and forming a small vessel from their lump, one should, in that little vessel, according to the previous method, put the mercury that has risen, leaving behind the copper, and also salt in the thirty-second part. After tying that little vessel in cloth, tying that cloth with a davaraka to a stick, and fastening that stick at the neck of the pot with some strip, one should put sour gruel mixed with one-third lemon juice into the pot; then the cloth-bound little vessel is to be suspended over the sour gruel, so that the sour gruel does not touch it and only the vapor touches it.
Then a fire should be kindled beneath the pot for a day and night.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi śigrupattrair navāṃ kulhaḍīṃ kṛtvā dolāyantreṇa tathaivāhorātraṃ rasaḥ svedanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, again making a new little vessel from <s>śigru</s> leaves, the mercury should be steamed in exactly the same way for a day and night by means of a <s>dolāyantra</s> (swing apparatus).

children.text: yadi cāgretanaṃ kāñjikaṃ śuṣyati tathā punarnavaṃ kāñjikaṃ kṣepyam ||
children.translated_text: And if the earlier sour gruel dries up, then fresh sour gruel should be added again.

children.text: evaṃ saptabhirdinaiḥ saptabhiḥ kulhaḍībhiḥ saptavāraṃ svedito rasaḥ sampratyūrdhvaṃ pacyamāno 'tyarthamagniṃ sahate ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in seven days, when the mercury has been steamed seven times with seven little vessels, from then onward, as it is cooked, it withstands fire exceedingly well.
Thus ends the seventh saṃskāra, the steaming of the raised mercury.
In another book, the steaming is as follows.

children.text: uttarasyāṃ diśi yaḥ sthūlo raktaḥ saindhavakhoṭako niṣpadyate ||
children.translated_text: In the northern region a large red lump of rock salt is produced.

children.text: tasya madhyāt kīye chidraṃ ca vidhāya sveditaṃ rasaṃ tatra kṣiptvopari caṇakakṣāro deyastata upari svalpo nimbukarasaḥ kṣepyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Making a hole of some size in the middle of it, one should put the steamed mercury there; chickpea alkali should be placed above it, and then a little lemon juice should be added above.

children.text: tatastasya chidrasyācchādanāyopari tādṛśa eva raktasaindhavakhoṭako deyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, to cover its hole, another red rock-salt lump of the same kind should be placed above.
Here the intention is this.

children.text: yāvanmātraṃ chidramadhaḥkhoṭake bhavati tāvatī bhūmir dvitīyakhoṭakasya madhye muktvoparitaḥ kiṃcid utkīryate ||
children.translated_text: As much as the hole is in the lower lump, that much area is left in the middle of the second lump, and a little is hollowed out above.
When that is placed on top, it becomes a rock-salt capsule.

children.text: tato bhūmau gajapramāṇāṃ gartāṃ kṛtvā tatra saindhavasampuṭaṃ muktvopary aṣṭāṅgulimānāṃ dhūliṃ dattvā chagaṇacūrṇena gartaṃ pūrayitvāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after making in the ground a pit of the measure of an elephant, placing the rock-salt capsule there, putting dust of eight finger-breadths above it, filling the pit with powdered goat dung, a fire should be kindled.

children.text: tataḥ prabhāte niṣkāsya kāñjikena prakṣālya punaḥ saindhavapuṭe kṣiptvopari navasāracūrṇaṃ nimbukarasaṃ ca muktvopari sampuṭaṃ ca dattvā punar gartāyāṃ muktvāhorātraṃ kārīṣāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, in the morning, after taking it out and washing it with sour gruel, one should again put it in a rock-salt enclosure, place powdered navasāra and lemon juice above, put the cover on top, place it again in the pit, and kindle a goat-dung fire for a day and night.
In this way it should be processed seven times, each time over seven days.
On the third day, sājī alkali is used.
On the fourth day, jhījarīṭa alkali is used.
On the fifth day hiṅgupuṣā is used, and on the sixth day and seventh day powdered castor fruit is used.
Lemon juice must indeed be added over all of them.
When this has been done, that regulating mercury withstands a very intense fire.
And, being somewhat hungry for moist food, it moves its tongue.
Thus ends the eighth saṃskāra, the regulating of the steamed mercury.

children.text: kācakumpikāyāṃ cikkaṇāṃ mṛdaṃ dattvā madhye niyāmakaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā mukhe koḍīyakam ||
children.translated_text: In a glass flask, after placing sticky clay and putting the regulating mercury in the middle, at the mouth there should be a koḍīyaka.
What is meant? One should put a potsherd plug.
After putting a cloth strip and clay above, one should dry it.

children.text: tato bhūmau gajapramāṇāṃ gartāṃ kṛtvā tatra kṣiptvopari aṣṭāṅgulidhūliṃ dattvāhorātraṃ kārīṣāgnirjvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, after making in the ground a pit of the measure of an elephant, placing it there, putting eight finger-breadths of dust above it, a goat-dung fire should be kindled for a day and night.

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ prabhāte rakṣāṃ kṛtvā navaṃ chagaṇacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvāhorātraṃ ca kārīṣāgnirjvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again in the morning, after making a protective sealing, fresh powdered goat dung should be added, and a goat-dung fire should be kindled for a day and night.

children.text: evaṃ saptabhir dinaiḥ saptavāraṃ saṃskṛto'sau nirodhako nāma raso mahābubhukṣayā pīḍito jihvāṃ lelihyamānaḥ kumpito grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when it has been processed seven times over seven days, that mercury called restraining mercury, afflicted by great hunger and licking its tongue, should be taken when it is trembling.
Thus ends the ninth saṃskāra, the restraining of the regulating mercury.

children.text: suniṣpannabījapūrasya vṛntam utpāṭya madhye utkīrya chidraṃ kṛtvā tato nirodhakaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvopari lavaṇaṃ muktvā punastena vṛntena chādayitvā bījapūrakaṃ vastre baddhvā tribhāgena nimbukarasayuktakāñjikabhṛtasthālī madhye dolāyantreṇa pūrvoktena kāñjike bruḍantaṃ bījapūrakaṃ dhṛtvādho 'gnir jvālanīyo 'horātram ||
children.translated_text: After plucking out the stalk of a well-ripened citron, hollowing out the middle and making a hole, one should put the restraining mercury there, place salt above it, cover it again with that stalk, tie the citron in cloth, and place the citron in the middle of a pot filled with sour gruel mixed with one-third lemon juice, by means of the previously described <s>dolāyantra</s>, with the citron immersed in the sour gruel; a fire should be kindled below for a day and night.

children.text: tataḥ punaḥ prabhāte navaṃ bījapūrakamānīya tathaiva madhye rasaṃ kṣiptvā dolāyantreṇāhorātraṃ rasaḥ saṃskāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again in the morning, bringing a fresh citron, one should put the mercury in its middle in the same way, and the mercury should be processed by the <s>dolāyantra</s> for a day and night.

children.text: evaṃ saptabhir dinaiḥ saptavāraṃ navanavair mātuluṅgaiḥ saṃskṛto raso dhānyābhrakādīnāṃ grasanāya prasāritamukho vidhinā dattaṃ sarvaṃ grāsaṃ jīryati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in seven days, when the mercury has been processed seven times with fresh citron fruits, its mouth extended for devouring dhānyābhraka and the like, it digests every morsel given according to rule.
Thus the tenth operation is the mouth-expansion processing of obstructing mercury.

children.text: iti dīpto viśuddhaḥ prabalataravidyucchaṭāsahasrābhaḥ sutarāṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus it becomes kindled, purified, and exceedingly like a thousand flashes of powerful lightning.
<s>Rasendra</s> (mercury), even in a substance, is to be employed in <s>rasāyana</s> (alchemy/rejuvenation).
Thus end the texts on kindling.

children.text: kācakumpikāmadhye prasāritamukhaṃ rasaṃ palam ekaṃ madhye muktvā kumpikāmukhe cātikāṃ dattvopari karpaṭamṛttikayā liptvā śoṣayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed one pala of mercury with its mouth expanded in the middle inside a glass flask, one should put a stopper at the mouth of the flask, smear it above with cloth and clay, and dry it.

children.text: tataḥ pṛthulamukhāyāṃ kuṇḍikāyāṃ vālukāṃ kṣiptvopari aṅgulacatuḥpañcapramāṇāṃ dhūliṃ dattvā kuṇḍikāyā adho 'ṣṭayāmān haṭhāgniṃ jvālayitvā dhānyābhrakapalaṃ jāraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after putting sand in a broad-mouthed pot and placing above it dust measuring four or five fingers, one should kindle a fierce fire below the pot for eight yāmas and digest one pala of dhānyābhraka mica.
Here, however, this is the transmitted instruction.

children.text: kuṇḍikāyāṃ tathā vālukā kṣepyā yathā tasyā upari kumpikāyāṃ muktāyāṃ tadupari aṅgulacatuḥpañcapramāṇāyāṃ vālukāyāṃ kṣiptāyāṃ kuṇḍikā pūrṇā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Sand should be put into the pot in such a way that, when the flask has been placed on it and sand measuring four or five fingers has been poured over that, the pot becomes full.

children.text: tathā rasapala 64 lavaṇapala 2 dhānyābhrakapala 1 iti mātrāpramāṇam ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, the prescribed measure is sixty-four palas of mercury, two palas of salt, and one pala of dhānyābhraka.

children.text: tatastāṃ kumpīm bhaṅktvā rasaṃ gṛhītvā punarapi dvitīyakumpikāyāṃ rasadhānyābhrakalavaṇanimbukarasān kṣiptvā pūrvavadahorātraṃ haṭhāgnijvālanena dhānyābhrakapalaṃ jāraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, having broken that flask and taken the mercury, one should again put the mercury, dhānyābhraka, salt, and lemon juice into a second flask, and, as before, digest one pala of dhānyābhraka by kindling a fierce fire for a day and night.

children.text: evamaṣṭabhir dinair aṣṭabhiḥ kumpikābhir aṣṭadhānyābhrakapalāni jāraṇīyāni ||
children.translated_text: In this way, over eight days, in eight flasks, eight palas of dhānyābhraka are to be digested.
Then that mercury is called <s>gaganagrāsa</s>.
Here is the transmitted instruction.

children.text: pūrvam abhrakair akhaṇḍavrīhibhiḥ ślakṣṇapāṣāṇakarkarair vādṛḍhanahīnavastrako thalikāṃ bhṛtvā dvāraṃ davarakeṇa dṛḍhaṃ baddhvā kāṣṭhapattrikāyāṃ jalapūrṇāyāṃ muktvā gāḍhaṃ tathā mardanīyo yathābhrakaṃ cūrṇībhūya kiṃcid bahir niḥsarati ||
children.translated_text: First, having filled a cloth-bag, neither too tight nor too loose, with pieces of mica like unbroken rice-grains and with smooth stone gravel, and having tied its opening firmly with a cord, one should place it in a wooden vessel filled with water and grind it hard, so that the mica is pulverized and a little comes out.
After drying that, the fine powder is taken.

children.text: idaṃ ca bhūmikāyāṃ kṣiptaṃ sūkṣmatvāt tatra lagati ||
children.translated_text: And when this is thrown on the ground, because of its fineness it adheres there.
Those who know mercury call this <s>dhānyābhraka</s>.

children.text: tathā pāradāddviguṇe dhānyābhrakeṇa jīrṇe'gniṃ tāpayettato raso dhūmena kṛtoḍḍīya yāti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when dhānyābhraka twice the quantity of mercury has been digested, if one heats the fire, then the mercury, having become smoke, flies away.

children.text: caturguṇe dhānyābhrake jīrṇe dhūmarūpeṇa na yāti ||
children.translated_text: When four times as much dhānyābhraka has been digested, it does not go away in the form of smoke.

children.text: kiṃtu haṭhāgniyoge mūṣāyām uḍḍīya bahiḥ patati ||
children.translated_text: But, when joined with a fierce fire in a crucible, it flies upward and falls outside.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇe dhānyābhrake jīrṇe bahiruḍḍīya na yāti ||
children.translated_text: When six times as much dhānyābhraka has been digested, it does not fly outward and go away.
Rather, it trembles inside the crucible.

children.text: aṣṭaguṇe jīrṇe haṭhena dhmāto hi suvarṇavat sthirībhavati na punaḥ punarmanāgapi kampate ||
children.translated_text: When eight times as much has been digested, and it has been forcibly blown upon, it becomes stable like gold and no longer trembles again even in the slightest.

children.text: tato mahāgnisahena tena rasena rūpyagadyāṇakapattram abhyañjya gālyate ||
children.translated_text: Then a sheet of silver gadyāṇaka is anointed with that mercury, which can withstand a great fire, and is melted.
At that time the gold becomes gold of ten-varṇa quality.

children.text: iti prasārite mukhasya rasasya gaganagrāsajāraṇaṃ prathamam ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first procedure, the gaganagrāsa-digestion of mercury whose mouth has been expanded.

children.text: yasmin lohakhalve catvāraḥ pādā mañcikayābhibhavanti sa catuṣpāda ucyate ||
children.translated_text: That iron mortar in which four feet are surmounted by a small stand is called four-footed.

children.text: tasmin lohakhalve grastābhrakasūtaṃ tathā catuḥṣaṣṭitamena sūtakasya kāntalohacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā yathā viḍena saha loṣṭikayā mandaṃ mandaṃ mandaṃ mardayet ||
children.translated_text: In that iron mortar, one should put mercury that has swallowed mica, and likewise magnetic iron powder in the sixty-fourth part of the mercury, and grind it gently, gently, gently with a lump together with the viḍa.
And below one should kindle a gentle fire.

children.text: evaṃ kurvatā yadi kāntalohacūrṇacatuḥṣaṣṭitamo jīrṇo bhavati tadā punarapi catuḥṣaṣṭitamabhāgena kāntalohacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā thūthāviḍena peṣaṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: While doing this, if the sixty-fourth part of magnetic iron powder becomes digested, then again one should add magnetic iron powder in a sixty-fourth part and grind it with thūthāviḍa.
And the fire below should be kindled.

children.text: evaṃ pūrvakṣipte lohacūrṇe jīrṇe punaḥ punas tāvac catuḥṣaṣṭitamāṃśena lohacūrṇaṃ kṣepyam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, when the iron powder previously added has been digested, iron powder should again and again be added in a sixty-fourth part,
until iron powder eight times the mercury has been digested.

children.text: ityarthaṃ lohacūrṇasya kaṣāyeṇa rasaḥ pāśitaḥ san godhūmavarṇo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: The meaning is that the mercury, bound by the astringent extract of the iron powder, becomes wheat-colored.
Likewise it is able to endure the rājis.
Next it digests prakāśa and the other rājis.

children.text: atra ca yadi kāntalohaṃ na labhyate tadā tīkṣṇāyasaṃ sāralohaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: And here, if magnetic iron is not obtained, then sharp iron and sāra iron may be used.

children.text: tathāyatvagheraṃ thūthakaṃ tat kāñjikena saṃghṛṣya candanaṃ kṣipyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, that thūthaka called ayatvaghera is rubbed with sour gruel, and sandalwood is added.
This is called <s>thūthāviḍa</s>.
Hereafter, everywhere the word thūthāviḍa should be understood as just this.
Thus ends the second procedure, the iron-digestion of mercury that has swallowed mica.

children.text: pūrvokte ca catuṣpāde lohakhalve jīrṇalohaṃ rasaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: And in the previously mentioned four-footed iron mortar, one should put mercury in which iron has been digested, and likewise

children.text: catuḥṣaṣṭitamabhāgena ayaḥprakāśirājicūrṇaṃ ca kṣiptvā pūrvoktena thūthāviḍena mardayet ||
children.translated_text: powder of ayaḥprakāśirāji in a sixty-fourth part, and grind it with the previously mentioned thūthāviḍa.
And below one should kindle a gentle fire.

children.text: agretanakṣiptāyaḥprakāśaṃ cūrṇe ca jīrṇe punas tāvanmātram ayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the previously added powder of ayaḥprakāśa has been digested, then again the same measure of ayaḥ should be added.

children.text: evaṃ ca yadi rasād aṣṭaguṇāyaḥprakāśarājijīrṇā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, if ayaḥprakāśarāji eight times the mercury has been digested,
then the mercury becomes yellow.

children.text: tataḥ sūtasya raktatānimittaṃ vakṣyamāṇarītyā hemarājiṃ jārayet ||
children.translated_text: After that, for the purpose of making the mercury red, one should digest hemarāji according to the method that will be stated.
Thus ends the third procedure, the digestion of ayaḥprakāśarāji for mercury in which iron has been digested.

children.text: rājisvarūpaṃ cāgre svayaṃ sa ca vyākhyāsyati ||
children.translated_text: And he himself will explain below the nature of rāji.

children.text: svarṇasyotpādanārthaṃ ca jāryaḥ śuddho hi gandhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And for the production of gold, purified sulfur indeed is to be digested.

children.text: yathā ayaḥprakāśarājirjāraṇā tathā hemarājerapi jāraṇā jñeyā ||
children.translated_text: Just as the digestion of ayahprakasharaji is done, so too the digestion of hemaraji should be understood.
And it is eight times the quantity of mercury; the rest is clear.
Thus the fourth operation: the digestion of hemaraji for mercury in which ayahprakashakaraji has been digested.

children.text: iha kūpavalloṣṭabandhaḥ kāñcikahastamāno garte sudhāyāś chohayā lipto yadi vāguḍaṃ sahitena cūrṇena liptaḥ śuṣkaḥ san ||
children.translated_text: Here, the sealing with a lump like a well: a pit, of the measure of a hand in sour gruel, is smeared with a coating of lime, or else smeared with powder mixed with jaggery, and then dried.
This apparatus is called <s>bhudhara</s>.

children.text: tataḥ kācaliptamṛttikākāṃsyaṃ śarāve jīrṇe hemarājiṃ sūtaṃ tathāṣoḍaśabhāgena śuddhagandhakacūrṇaṃ vā kṣiptvopari mukhakācaliptamṛttikākoḍīyakaṃ dattvā karpaṭamṛttikayā liptvā taṃ śarāvaṃ sampuṭaṃ bhūdharayantramadhye muktvā haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should put into an earthen-bronze dish smeared with glass either the mercury in which hemaraji has been digested, and likewise purified sulphur powder in one-sixteenth part; placing over it a small earthen cup smeared at the mouth with glass, coating it with cloth and clay, setting that lidded dish in the middle of the <s>bhudhara</s> apparatus, a strong fire should be kindled.
And the nature of purified sulphur must be learned from the mouth of a teacher.

children.text: yataḥ sarvasminn apyatra granthe 'nyatrāpi ca śuddhagandhaka eva kīcanasi dvimūlabījam ||
children.translated_text: For everywhere in this whole book, and elsewhere too, only purified sulphur is the double root-seed in kicanasi.

children.text: ata eva sarvatra gandhakaśuddhiyuktir gopitaiṣeti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore it should be known that the method for purifying sulphur has everywhere been kept secret.

children.text: sadoṣe ca gandhake jārite na kāryasiddhiriti tu gurumukhād gandhakaśuddhir avagantavyā ||
children.translated_text: And if sulphur with defects is digested, the desired result is not attained; therefore the purification of sulphur must be learned from the mouth of a teacher.

children.text: tathā pūrvakṣiptagandhakaṣoḍaśabhāge jīrṇe punaḥ koḍīyakamūrchāyāśugandhakaṣoḍaśabhāgaṃ kṣiptvā koḍīyakaṃ dattvā haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when the previously added one-sixteenth part of sulphur has been digested, again one should add one-sixteenth part of swift sulphur for the stupor of the small cup, place the cup on it, and kindle a strong fire.

children.text: evaṃ ca rasāt ṣaḍguṇaśuddhagandhake jīrṇe 'tīvaraktaḥ pārado bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this way, when purified sulphur six times the amount of the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) has been digested, the mercury becomes very red.

children.text: tena ca rasena rūpyaṃ tāmraṃ lohaṃ vaṅgaṃ nāgaṃ pittalaṃ kāṃsyaṃ ceti sapta lohāni abhyañjya gālitāni pañcadaśasuvarṇāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: And when seven metals, namely silver, copper, iron, tin, lead, brass, and bronze, are anointed with that <s>rasa</s> and melted, they become fifteen suvarnas.
Thus the fifth operation: sulphur digestion for mercury in which hemaraji has been digested.
Here, chalk.
Salt.
Turi.

children.text: gairikavarṇikājīkaka ityetābhiḥ pañcabhir mṛttikābhiḥ parīkṣakāḥ kanakaṃ parīkṣyaṃ tena yathā ||
children.translated_text: With these five earths, namely gairika, varnika, ajika, and the others, assayers test gold as follows.

children.text: kanakapattrāṇi kāñjikena kledayitvā rajakatyaktatūrīśuṣkalagadakaṃ lavaṇena samabhāgena cūrṇayitvā karparaḥ paricūrṇas tadupari pattraṃ punaścūrṇaṃ punaḥ pattramevaṃ pattrāṇy uparyupari muktvopari punaḥ karparaṃ dattvā cūrṇena sarvataḥ pārśve vācchādya yāvadbhiḥ karparapuṭa ācchādyate tāvanti chagaṇakāni khaḍakitvāgni dattvā mucyate yadi ca jvalitvā svayaṃ tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Having moistened gold leaves with sour gruel, one should powder dried lagadaka and turi discarded by a washerman with an equal part of salt; then a potsherd is powdered, a leaf is placed upon that, then powder, then again a leaf. Thus, placing the leaves one above another, putting another potsherd over them, covering them on all sides and at the edges with the powder, as many cow-dung cakes as are needed for the potsherd heating are piled up, fire is applied, and it is left until, after burning, it stops by itself.

children.text: tadā punar dvitīyavāraṃ chagaṇakhaṇḍakapūrṇaḥ puṭo deyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a second heating should again be given, filled with pieces of cow-dung cake.

children.text: evaṃ yadi malādhikyaṃ tadā tṛtīyo deyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If in this way there is an excess of impurity, then a third should be given.

children.text: evaṃ citrakṣaṭakhaṭikayāpi golakakhaṭikayā vā lavaṇamiśrayāpi puṭadvayatrayadānena tadeva kāryam ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, the very same operation should be done with citraksata chalk, or with ball-chalk mixed with salt, by giving two or three heatings.
Now, if this is known:

children.text: evaṃ kṛte'pi sarvathā na śuddhaṃ dravyaṃ yadi vāvadūlotādikudhātumasādhikyaṃ tadāmasavāravarṇikayā jīkakeṇa vā lavaṇamiśreṇa pūrvarītyaiva puṭadvayatrayadāne sarvamalaśuddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Even after this has been done, if the substance is still not purified in every respect, or if there is an excess of bad-metal impurity such as avadulota, then by varnika that removes impurity, or by jika mixed with salt, all impurity is purified by giving two or three heatings in just the earlier manner.
Thus there is purification of all defects by means of the five earths.

children.text: tathā caturdaśavaṇikādaśīkādaśayanavāś ceti sampratikale svarṇaparamasīmā ataḥ paraṃ śodhane 'pi kṛte na hi karṇikāvṛddhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, fourteen vanikas, ten sikas, and ten yanas are the present highest limit of gold; beyond that, even when purification is performed, there is no increase of the karnika.

children.text: tathā śodhanacūrṇaṃ yadi dhmāyate tadā yo rūpyādidhātuś cīrṇo bhavati so 'pi labhyate ||
children.translated_text: And if the purifying powder is smelted, then whatever metal such as silver has been absorbed is also obtained.

children.text: tathā rūpyaṃ karpare kṣiptvoparisīsakaṃ kṣipyate'dho jālyate tato dvāv api sarāvedākatra bhūtvā bhramatas tadāvasīsakarajatamalaṃ caritvā karparalagitāgaraṇarakṣāṅgulapramāṇaś caramadhye milati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, silver is put in a potsherd, lead is thrown over it, and it is heated from below; then when both have become one mass in the dish and are turning about, at that time the lead, having consumed the impurity of the silver, gathers in the middle, the protective coating stuck to the potsherd being of the measure of a finger.

children.text: śuddharūpyarasaśca yadi bhrāntas tiṣṭhati tadā jñeyaṃ śuddho rūpyarasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if the purified silver-rasa remains moving about, then it should be known to be purified silver-rasa.
When the protective coating has been examined, the metals are obtained in the earth that has been consumed.
These and similar matters are to be understood from the mouths of experts.
Now the explanation of the root text.

children.text: bhūdharayantre śarāvasampuṭe jīrṇaṃ gandhakaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā dvātriṃśattamena manaḥśilāsattvaṃ ca kṣiptvā mukhe koḍīyakaṃ dattvā karpaṭamṛttikayā ca liptvā haṭhāgniṃ jvālayet jīrṇe ca manaḥśilāsattve punardvātriṃśattamena bhāgena tasya kṣepaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In a lidded dish within the <s>bhudhara</s> apparatus, having put <s>rasa</s> in which sulphur has been digested, one should add realgar essence in a thirty-second part, place a small cup at the mouth, coat it with cloth and clay, and kindle a strong fire; when the realgar essence has been digested, again a portion of it, in a thirty-second part, is to be added.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṣepaṇasūtatulyaṃ manaḥśilāsattvaṃ jāryam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by adding it again and again, realgar essence equal to the mercury is to be digested.
It should be neither deficient nor excessive.

children.text: evaṃ manaḥśilāsattve jīrṇe pāradena saptalohānyabhyaṅgagālitāni hemarūpāṇi bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: When realgar essence has thus been digested, the seven metals, anointed with mercury and melted, become forms of gold.

children.text: tacca hema pañcabhir mṛttikābhiḥ śodhanikāṃ sahate ||
children.translated_text: And that gold withstands purification by the five earths.
Likewise it becomes pure through the first cutting, kasavarta, and purification procedures.
Thus the sixth operation: the digestion of realgar essence for mercury in which sulphur has been digested.

children.text: etāvadbhiḥ saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛto raso lohasādhaka eva ||
children.translated_text: By so many processes the treated <s>rasa</s> is only effective for accomplishing metals.

children.text: ataḥ paraṃ ca ye saṃskārā yāni ca jāraṇāni tāni dehalohasādhakānīti ||
children.translated_text: Beyond this, the processes and digestions that follow are effective for accomplishing both the body and metals.
There he states the seventh procedure, the digestion of khāparasattva.

children.text: catuṣpāde lohaṣairaleṣāparasūtvaṃ tasmāccatuḥṣaṣṭiguṇaṃ jīrṇamanaḥśilāsattvaṃ pāradaṃ ca kṣiptvā thūthāviḍena saṃpiṣann adho mṛduvahnir jvālayet ||
children.translated_text: In an iron mortar standing on four feet, having put in mercury together with digested realgar essence sixty-four times its measure, one should grind it with thūthāviḍa and kindle a gentle fire below.

children.text: atratane ca khāparasattve jīrṇe bhāgena tadeva kṣepyam ||
children.translated_text: And when the khāparasattva added here has been digested, that same substance should be added by measure.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṣiptvā rasādaṣṭaguṇaṃ khāparasattvaṃ jāraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, adding it again and again, khāparasattva eight times the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is to be digested.

children.text: tataḥ pāradaḥ sasneho vā saṃpratyūrdhvam annapathahīrakaṃ jīryati ||
children.translated_text: Then the mercury, being oily, now digests annapatha diamond.
Thus the seventh procedure, the digestion of khāparasattva for that mercury in which realgar essence has been digested.
Below he will explain the production of annapatha diamonds in three ways.

children.text: tatas teṣāṃ prakāratrayāṇāṃ madhyātprathamamekatamena prakāreṇa niṣpannam annapathe hīrakabhasma tathā jīrṇakhāparasattvaṃ sutaṃ cobhāv api catuṣpāde lohakhalve kṣiptvā thūthāviḍena piṣan kharalādho bhāge komalāgniṃ jvālayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, from among those three methods, having put into a four-footed iron mortar diamond ash produced by one of the first methods in annapatha, and also mercury in which khāparasattva has been digested, one should grind both with thūthāviḍa and kindle a gentle fire beneath the mortar.
This is done until all the diamond ash is digested.

children.text: tato hīrake jīrṇe sati rasaḥ sarvavyāpīti dehalohavyāpako bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the diamond has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> becomes all-pervading, that is, capable of pervading the body and metals.
Thus the eighth procedure, the digestion of annapatha diamond into mercury in which khāparasattva has been digested.
Now, according to another view, the viḍas.
Now he states the means of knowing whether the substances to be digested have been digested or not digested.
Here too this is the transmitted teaching.

children.text: ihānantaraproktaṃ dhānyābhrakādīnām sa ca tameṣv anyeṣu vastuṣu rase jāriteṣu sasūtakaṃ jīrṇam ajīrṇam eveti vicāraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, after substances such as the just-mentioned dhānyābhraka and the others have been digested in <s>rasa</s>, there is the examination whether it, together with the mercury, is digested or still undigested.

children.text: prathamo garbhaḥ dvitīyaḥ piṇḍastṛtīyaḥ pariṇāmaka iti trividhaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: There are three kinds of signs: first garbha, second piṇḍa, and third pariṇāmaka.

children.text: tadyathā jāryaṃ vastu jārayitvā raso vastreṇa gālyate tato yadi kiṃcidvastre śeṣaṃ vigālya tiṣṭhati tadā jñeyo'sau garbha iti ||
children.translated_text: That is as follows: after digesting the substance to be digested, the <s>rasa</s> is filtered through a cloth. If anything remains in the cloth and stays there without filtering through, that should be known as garbha.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi saraś carubhyate tadeva kharale kṣiptvā yathā viḍena peṣitāgnirjvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again the <s>rasa</s> is to be processed: putting that same substance into the mortar, one should kindle fire after grinding it with the viḍa as before.

children.text: ayaṃ bhāvo jāraṇā yena vidhinā pūrvaṃ bhaṇitāsti sā tena vidhinā jāryauṣadhaṃ vinaivānumānena taptvā punarvastreṇa raso gālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sense is this: the digestion that was previously taught should be heated again in that same manner, but without the drug to be digested, according to judgment; then the <s>rasa</s> should again be filtered through a cloth.

children.text: tato yadi vastrātpūrvo 'pi niḥsarati nanu kiṃcil lagati paraṃ tolitaḥ sa tu nijataulyādhiko bhavati tadā jñeyo'sau piṇḍa iti ||
children.translated_text: Then, if it comes out from the cloth as before, and although a little clings to it, when weighed it is greater than its own former weight, that should be known as piṇḍa.
The meaning is that the drug is still not completely digested.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi yathā bhaṇitāsti tathaiva jāryauṣadhopakṣepeṇa vinaiva vidhāpunar navavastreṇa raso gālyate ||
children.translated_text: Then again, just as has been stated, without another addition of the drug to be digested and by the same method, the <s>rasa</s> is again filtered through a new cloth.

children.text: yadi vastrānniḥsṛto gālitaḥ sannijataulye tiṣṭhati tadā jñeyo'sau pariṇāmaka iti ||
children.translated_text: If, having come out of the cloth and been filtered, it remains at its own weight, that should be known as pariṇāmaka.
The meaning is that the drug has been entirely digested by the <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: atrādyam etad dvayameva śuddhakṛto yo bhedaḥ śuddhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, the first two alone are a distinction made for purification; the purified state is the latter.
Thus the section on the signs of digestion of substances to be digested.
Thus the sāraṇa is completed.
Thus, by these eight processes, the eleventh process, digestion, is completed.

children.text: iha kumbhasya tale chidram aṅgulipraveśayogyaṃ kṛtvā tatra davarakaṃ kṣiptvā madhye bahirapi ca davarake granthiṃ dattvā tathā kāryaṃ yathā satkumbho galadghaṭī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Here, having made a hole in the bottom of a pot, fit for the entry of a finger, one should insert a davaraka there and tie knots in the davaraka both in the middle and outside, arranging it so that the good pot becomes a dripping vessel.
The meaning is that the medicinal <s>rasa</s> placed in it drips down.

children.text: tataḥ sthālikāmadhye jīrṇadorakaṃ pāradaṃ kṣiptvā upari sacchidrā pradhvarā ḍhaṅkaṇī dīyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, having placed mercury in which doraka has been digested in the middle of a cooking vessel, a sloping lid with a hole is put over it.

children.text: tasyāścopari galadghaṭī kumbhomumutkā mahoḍākamūlānāṃ śrīṣaṇḍena sakumbho bhriyate ||
children.translated_text: And above that lid, the dripping vessel, namely the pot with its mouth upward, is filled with śrīṣaṇḍa of mahoḍāka roots.

children.text: tataḥ sthālikāyā adhastāc caturo yāmān haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a strong fire should be kindled below the cooking vessel for four yāmas.

children.text: evaṃ ca yathā yathā kumbhamadhyāḍḍhaṅkaṇī chidreṇa davarakād galitvā tuṣarasaḥ pārade patati tathā tathāgnidagdhaḥ pāradaḥ śvetabhasma bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And in this way, as the juice of the chaff, dripping from the davaraka through the hole in the lid from within the pot, falls onto the mercury, so the mercury, burned by the fire, becomes white ash.

children.text: tataśca tatsūtabhasma madhvājyaṭaṅkaṇaiḥ sākaṃ bandhamūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā dhmāyate ||
children.translated_text: Then that ash of mercury is placed together with honey, ghee, and borax in a sealed crucible and is blown upon.
Then the mercury, after being smelted, becomes bound.

children.text: ko 'rthaḥ anekaśo 'tyarthaṃ dhmāto'pi niścalo bhavati na punaḥ kṣīyate ||
children.translated_text: What does this mean? Even when smelted many times and very intensely, it remains motionless and is not diminished again.

children.text: yaḥ pārado jāryamāṇaḥ san badhyate svayameva nibadhyate nirāyāsabaddho bhavati sa hi siddharasa ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: Mercury which, while being digested, becomes bound, indeed binds itself of its own accord and becomes bound without effort; that is called siddharasa.
And it is able to pierce bodies and metals.
Therefore this siddharasa has been produced by the method stated above.
Now he states the result of siddharasa.
It is applied to the eyes of a deer with non-black <s>rasa</s>.
Pain in the eyes disappears.
When siddharasa collyrium is applied to blind eyes, the blind person sees.

children.text: tathā yasya mukhe siddharasaguṭikā tiṣṭhati tasyākāśe gatir devadānavagandharvasiddhayakṣakhecarair na hanyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, one in whose mouth a pill of siddharasa remains has motion in the sky and is not slain by gods, demons, gandharvas, siddhas, yakṣas, or sky-goers.

children.text: tathā siddharase mukhe sthite viṣeṇa na mriyate ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when siddharasa is held in the mouth, one does not die from poison.
One is not burned by fire.
And in the sky one becomes possessed of the knowledge of siddharasa.
A dead person, being unconscious, comes to life at that very moment.
Likewise, even more than jewels, mantras, and great medicines, the exceptional power of perfected <s>rasa</s> is very great.
This <s>rasabandha</s> (binding of mercury) is called <s>mṛtajīvana</s>, reviving the dead.
What is meant? One who is as if dead is called dead.

children.text: sarpadaṃśavahnidāhajalaplāvaśastraghātaviṣādiduṣṭaprayogair mūrchitaḥ yaḥ kenāpi jīvayituṃ na śakyate so 'pi mukhe kṣiptasyāsya rasasya prabhāveṇa kṣaṇād eva jīvati ||
children.translated_text: Someone who has fainted from snakebite, burning by fire, drowning in water, a blow from a weapon, poison, or other harmful applications, and who cannot be revived by anyone, even he lives at once through the power of this <s>rasa</s> when it is placed in his mouth.
Thus ends the twelfth operation, the binding procedure of mercury in which diamond has been digested.

children.text: pūrvoktayuktyā baddhasūtasya catuḥṣaṣṭipalāni gālayitvā tato dvitīyamuṣāyāṃ hemarājicatuḥṣaṣṭipalāni gālayet ||
children.translated_text: Having melted sixty-four palas of bound mercury by the method stated earlier, one should then melt sixty-four palas of <s>hemarāji</s> in a second crucible.
Then those sixty-four palas of melted <s>hemarāji</s> are to be poured over the sixty-four palas of melted bound mercury.
Then the two, having joined together, become a red lump.
This is called the <s>sāraṇa</s> operation.
Thus ends the thirteenth operation, <s>sāraṇa</s> of bound mercury.

children.text: iha sāraṇasaṃskāre kṛte yāvanto raktaṣoṭasya gadyāṇā bhavanti tebhyo dviguṇāttu śuddhamanaḥśilāgadyāṇān gāḍhaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇarūpān kṛtvā prauḍhakācakūpīmadhye 'rdhacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tato raktaṣoṭaṃ muktvā punarupari śeṣaṃ manaḥśilācūrṇam adhaḥ kṣiptvā kūpīmadhye'dhaścūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā tato raktaṣoṭaṃ muktvā punarupari śeṣaṃ manaḥśilācūrṇamadhaḥ liptvā kūpīdvāre 'bhrasya cātikāṃ dattvā saptatāraṃ tasyāṃ kūpikāyāṃ paritaḥ karpaṭamṛttikāṃ dattvāraṇyachāṇakaiḥ pūrṇāyāṃ puruṣapramāṇakhanitagartāyāṃ madhye kūpīṃ muktvā haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, when the <s>sāraṇa</s> operation has been performed, however many gadyāṇas of the red lump there are, one should take twice as many gadyāṇas of purified realgar, make it firmly into a fine powder, put half the powder into a mature glass bottle, then place in the red lump, and again put the remaining realgar powder above it; after placing powder below in the bottle and then the red lump, and again smearing the remaining realgar powder below, one should put a mica stopper at the mouth of the bottle, apply cloth and clay around that little bottle seven times, place the bottle in the middle of a pit dug to the measure of a man and filled with forest cow-dung cakes, and kindle a violent fire.

children.text: yadi ca jvalitā svayaṃ śītalaṃ bhavati tadā kūpīmadhyāt sa raso grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And if, after burning, it becomes cool by itself, then that <s>rasa</s> should be taken from inside the bottle.
This is called <s>māraṇa</s> (killing or calcination).
Here is the traditional instruction.

children.text: khaḍḍāyām ardhaṃ yāvacchaṇakāni muktvopari kūpī mucyate tataḥ pārśveṣattathopari chāṇakair gartā bhriyate ||
children.translated_text: After cow-dung cakes have been placed up to half of the pit, the bottle is placed above; then the pit is filled with cow-dung cakes at the sides and above.
Thus ends the fourteenth operation, the <s>māraṇa</s> of extracted mercury.

children.text: iha manusaṃkhyaiś caturdaśabhiḥ saṃskārair anantaroktaiḥ saṃskṛtya yo māritasūtaḥ sukhalve kṣiptvātyarthaṃ piṣyate ||
children.translated_text: Here the killed mercury, after being processed by the fourteen operations, numbered like <s>Manu</s>, that have just been stated, is placed in a good mortar and ground very thoroughly.
This is called <s>pratisāraṇa</s>.
Thus ends the fifteenth operation, <s>pratisāraṇa</s> of killed mercury.

children.text: iha mṛtasīsakena kāñcanaṃ sārayitvā tasya mṛtakāñcanasya cūrṇaṃ yat pratisāritarase kṣipyate ||
children.translated_text: Here, after gold has been extracted with killed lead, the powder of that killed gold is put into the <s>rasa</s> that has undergone <s>pratisāraṇa</s>.
This is called <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
Thus ends the sixteenth operation, <s>krāmaṇa</s> of mercury that has undergone <s>pratisāraṇa</s>.
And he himself will state below the procedure for killing lead and gold.

children.text: iha prathamaṃ śuddhanāgasyaikena patre'vadyena patraṃ kṛtvā tatra ratimātraṃ kramitaṃ rasaṃ kṣiptvā nārāpatrasthātanu gālayitvā veḍhanīṃ ca kṛtvā tāṃ veḍhanīṃ gālayet ||
children.translated_text: Here first, making a sheet from one uncut sheet of purified lead, one should place there a rati measure of <s>krāmita rasa</s>, melt the thin metal from the lead sheet, make a covering, and melt that covering.
Then it becomes a powder.

children.text: tataḥ pūrvoktāni sarvāṇyapi nāgavaṅgādilohāni ratisahasramātrāṇi gālayitvā bhramatyeva loharase ratimātraṃ veḍhanīrasaṃ cūrṇaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then one should melt all the previously mentioned metals, beginning with lead and tin, in a quantity of one thousand ratis; while the metallic liquid is still moving, one should throw in a rati measure of the powdered covering-<s>rasa</s>.
Then the gold stuck at the bottom should be taken.
This is the <s>rasa</s> that pierces a thousandfold.
Thus ends the seventeenth operation, the <s>vedhaka</s> procedure of mercury that has undergone <s>krāmaṇa</s>.
Then, into the middle of that powder, one gadyāṇaka of sulfur is to be put.
And one gadyāṇaka of <s>sarjikā</s> is to be added.

children.text: tato gālitanāgagadyāṇakaḥ 1 sūtagadyāṇakaḥ 2 gandhakagadyāṇakaḥ 1 evaṃ gadyāṇakacatuṣṭayaṃ melayitvā gāḍhaṃ sampiṣya cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā jalenāloḍayitvā punaḥ śoṣayitvā tataḥ śarāvasampuṭe kṣiptvā sampuṭasaṃdhau ca vastramṛttikāṃ dattvā tato hastapramāṇāyāṃ gartāyāṃ madhye chāṇakāni kṣiptvopari śarāvasampuṭaṃ dattvā muktvā punaḥ pārśveṣūpari chāṇakaiḥ khaṇḍībhūtvāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, combining one gadyāṇaka of melted lead, two gadyāṇakas of mercury, and one gadyāṇaka of sulfur, thus four gadyāṇakas in all, one should grind them firmly, make a powder, stir it with water, dry it again, then put it into a lidded earthen dish; after applying cloth and clay at the joint of the lid, one should place cow-dung cakes in the middle of a pit measuring a hand, put the lidded dish above them, and again kindle the fire after filling the sides and top with cow-dung cakes in pieces.

children.text: yadi ca jvalitvā na svayaṃ sthito bhavati tadā sampuṭamadhyād auṣadhaṃ gṛhītvā sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ kṛtvā vedhasaṃskṛtasya gālitasya rasasya madhye sarṣapamātraṃ gadyāṇacatuṣṭayaṃ sūkṣmacūrṇaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: And if, after burning, it has not stopped by itself, then one should take the medicine from inside the lidded dish, make it into a fine powder, and put a mustard-seed-sized amount of the fine powder of four gadyāṇakas into the melted <s>rasa</s> processed by the piercing operation.

children.text: atra ca sūtamadhye kṣepyauṣadhasya pramāṇaṃ bhaṇitam ||
children.translated_text: Here the measure of the medicine to be put into the mercury has been stated.
But not the measure for the pierced <s>rasa</s>.
Nor has its measure been stated by the teachers.
Therefore it is understood to be by inference.
Afterwards, everywhere, sixty-four palas of <s>rasa</s> are prescribed.

children.text: tatastāvatā rasena yāvadauṣadhaṃ vedhasaṃskāre kriyamāṇe niṣpannaṃ tāvat evauṣadhasya rasasya madhye gadyāṇakacatuṣṭayaṃ pūrṇaṃ sarṣapamātraṃ kṣeptavyam ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, with that much <s>rasa</s>, as much medicine as has been produced when the piercing operation is being performed, exactly that complete quantity of four gadyāṇakas of the medicine is to be put into the <s>rasa</s> in a mustard-seed-sized amount.
In daylight, by the command of the venerable teacher, one knows the proper measure.

children.text: evaṃ sarṣapamātre cūrṇe kṣipte viddhasūtasyodghāṭanaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When powder of a mustard-seed measure has thus been added, the opening of the pierced mercury occurs.
<s>Udghāṭana</s>, opening, means piercing all metals and removing all diseases.
Thus the eighteenth <s>saṃskāra</s> (procedure).

children.text: iha mānaśulbaṃ mārayitvā punar jīvyate taṃ jīvantaṃ śulvaṃ kathayanti ||
children.translated_text: Here, after killing māna-śulba, it is brought to life again; they call that living śulva.

children.text: tatastacchulbasyaiko bhāgaḥ tathā dvau hemabhāgau evaṃ bhāgatrayaṃ gālayitvā iti tat sthūlaṃ pattraṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Then one part of that śulba, and likewise two parts of gold, thus three parts in all, should be melted down, and from it one should make a thick sheet.

children.text: tato manaḥśilāyāṃ nimbukarasaiśca nāgaṃ mārayitvā jatupattram ubhayapārśvayos tena māritanāgena lepanīyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after killing lead with realgar and lemon juices, the lac sheet is to be smeared on both sides with that killed lead.

children.text: tataścitrakūṭakhaṭīlavaṇayoḥ samabhāgena cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā sthālīṃ bhṛtvā tasya madhye ūrdhvaṃ bruḍantaṃ pattraṃ muktvā mukhe'dhomukhaṃ śarāvaṃ kṛtvā sādha kaṇṭhe mṛdā liptvā śarāvasyoparyadhomukhaṃ ḍhaṅkaṇīṃ dattvā sthālikādhaḥ praharacatuṣkaṃ yāvat haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made a powder from equal parts of citrakūṭa and khaṭī salt, one should fill a pot, place the sheet upright in the middle, make an inverted saucer over the mouth, seal it at the neck with clay, place an inverted lid above the saucer, and kindle a forceful fire beneath the pot for four praharas.

children.text: evaṃ ca kṛte pattrasya phāḍītrayaṃ jāyate ||
children.translated_text: And when this has been done, the sheet becomes three flakes.

children.text: tato yā madhyamā phāḍī tāṃ gṛhītvā mardanīyaṃ pārśvaphāḍīdvayam ca tyajanīyaṃ yacca madhyaphāḍīcūrṇaṃ sā hemarājir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: Then the middle flake should be taken and ground, while the two side flakes should be discarded; the powder of the middle flake is called hemarāji.

children.text: tasya catuḥṣaṣṭitamo bhāgaḥ pūrvoktayuktyā pūrvaproktasya rasasya dātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: One sixty-fourth part of it is to be given to the previously described <s>rasa</s> (mercury) by the method stated before.

children.text: evaṃ tāvadyāvadaṣṭaguṇo hemarājiṃ dattvā pūrvoktarītyā jāritā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: This is done until, after hemarāji has been given eightfold, it has been digested by the method stated above.
Thus the excellent hemarāji is completed.

children.text: iha yā nāgarājiḥ sā sāmānyā svalpakāryakārī ||
children.translated_text: Here, that nāgarāji is ordinary and accomplishes only a small task.
The mākṣikarāji accomplishes a middling task.
The vyoṣarāji is excellent and accomplishes many tasks.

children.text: ayaḥprakāśarājistābhyaḥ sarvābhyo rājibhya uttamā sarvottamakārīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The ayaḥprakāśarāji is better than all those rājis, meaning that it accomplishes the very best result.
Therefore the ayaḥprakāśarāji is stated first.
One pala of sāra iron and two palas of bronze;
nine palas of purified copper and three palas of brass;
fifteen palas of lead killed with realgar.
Thus, thirty palas as the full total should be put into a crucible and melted.

children.text: tataḥ suvarṇamākṣikasya sārdhasaptapalānyānīya stokena madhye kṣiptvā punaḥ śanaistāvadāvartanīyāni yāvatā tāmrabhāgapramāṇāni bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Then, having brought seven and a half palas of gold-mākṣika, one should throw it little by little into the middle and again melt it slowly until it becomes equal to the measure of the copper portion.
This is the meaning.
There are nine palas of copper.

children.text: tataḥ sarvo rasa āvartayitvā yadā navapalapramāṇo bhavati tadā prathamāsāv ayaḥprakāśarājiḥ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when all the <s>rasa</s> has been melted and becomes a measure of nine palas, then this first one is called ayaḥprakāśarāji.
Thus the supreme ayaḥprakāśarāji is described.

children.text: sāralohacūrṇaṃ kāṃsyacūrṇaṃ ca samamātrayā mūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā tata āvartya ekapiṇḍaṃ kriyate ||
children.translated_text: Powder of sāra iron and powder of bronze, in equal quantity, are placed in a crucible; then, after melting them, one lump is made.

children.text: tatastasmātpiṇḍād ardhamātrayā śuddhanāgaṃ madhye kṣiptvā mūṣāyāṃ punaḥ punarāvartya jāraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: Then purified lead, in half the measure of that lump, is put into the middle and is to be digested in the crucible by melting it again and again.
Then lead, again in half the measure, is put in and digested.

children.text: yadi caivaṃ punaḥ punarjāraṇena kāṃsyāt ṣaḍguṇaṃ nāgaṃ jīrṇaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And if, by repeated digestion in this way, lead six times the bronze is digested,
then vyoṣarāji is produced.
Thus vyoṣarāji means bronze-rāji.

children.text: prathamaṃ śuddhatāmrasya catvāri palāni pṛthag āvartayitvā tatastanmadhye thūthāpalāni catvāri catvāri mākṣīkapalānyevamaṣṭau palāni cūrṇīkṛtya stokena stokena kṣiptvā punaḥ punarāvartya tāvajjārayet ||
children.translated_text: First, four palas of purified copper should be melted separately; then, into the middle of it, four palas of thūthā and four palas of mākṣika, thus eight palas, are powdered, thrown in little by little, and repeatedly melted and digested.
This is done until only the copper remains.
The meaning is that all the medicine, four palas, is digested.
Thus the mākṣikarāji is the third.

children.text: śuddhatāmrasya bhāgamekaṃ mūṣāyāṃ gālayitvā tato manaḥśilāyā bhāgāś catvāro mṛtanāgasya bhāgāstathā catvāraḥ tathā catvāraḥ thūthābhāgāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having melted one part of purified copper in a crucible, then four parts of realgar, likewise four parts of dead lead, and also four parts of thūthā are taken.

children.text: evaṃ dvādaśabhāgāṃścūrṇīkṛtya stokena śulvamadhye kṣiptvā tāvadāvartayed yāvattāmraśeṣaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having powdered the twelve parts, one should put them little by little into the śulva and melt them until only the copper remains.
This is called nāgarāji.

children.text: thūthānāgarājīnāṃ phalamāha rājyabhyucchritalohānām ityādi catasṛṇāmapi rājīnāṃ lohasya cūrṇaṃ kṛtvaikaikarājiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He states the result of the thūthā- and nāga-rājis: beginning with 'of the metals raised up by rāji,' of all four rājis too, after making the metal into powder, each rāji is applied.
In mercury it is to be digested eightfold, by the mercury method stated above, in sequence; this is the procedure for making rāji.
Thus the nāgarāji is the fourth.

children.text: rasakasya khāparasya maṇamekaṃ naramūtreṇa dinatrayaṃ kvāthayitvā ātape dattvā śoṣayitvā praharamekaṃ dugdhena pācayitvā punaḥ śoṣayitvā cūrṇīkṛtya tanmadhye'ṣṭabhāgena khalaścaturthabhāgena ṭaṅkaṇakṣāro'ṣṭamabhāgena pūrvaguḍa etāni trīṇi kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: One maṇa of rasaka khāpara should be boiled for three days in human urine, placed in the sun and dried, cooked for one prahara with milk, dried again, and powdered; into it one should put these three: khala in an eighth part, borax alkali in a fourth part, and old jaggery in an eighth part.

children.text: tato mṛttikayā mūṣādvayaṃ kaccolakasamānaṃ prauḍhaṃ vartulākāraṃ kṛtvā ekasyāṃ mūṣāyāṃ pūrvoktakhāparacūrṇaṃ kṣiptvā sā mūṣādhomukhī nālopari moktavyā ||
children.translated_text: Then two crucibles of clay, strong, round in shape, and equal to small bowls, should be made; the previously described khāpara powder should be placed in one crucible, and that crucible, mouth downward, is to be set upon a tube.

children.text: tataḥ karpaṭamṛttikayā sarvapārśveṣu niśchidraṃ vidhāya sattvapātanāya īdṛśas tumbanalīnāmā yantraḥ kartavyaḥ tataḥ koṭhīmadhye babbūlakhadiram āmbalīprabhṛtīnāṃ līhālakaiḥ pūrayitvā yantraṃ ca tatra kṣiptvā punaḥ punar dhmātvā saṃdaṃśair adhomukhīṃ yantranalīṃ dhṛtvā yāvanmātro raso madhyād galitvādhomūṣāyāṃ sameti tat khāparasattvaṃ kathyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made it without openings on all sides with cloth and clay, for the falling of the essence an apparatus of this kind, called tumbanalī, should be made. Then, after filling the furnace chamber with the līhālakas of babbūla, khadira, āmbalī, and the like, and placing the apparatus there, one should blow again and again; holding the tube of the apparatus downward with tongs, whatever amount of <s>rasa</s> has melted out from the middle and collects in the lower crucible is called khāparasattva.
Thus the procedure for extracting khāparasattva.

children.text: sarvottamā kaṇayarī manaḥśilā kharale piṣṭvā kumpe kṣiptvā abhrakeṇa kumpamukhaṃ pidhāya lavaṇasahitaṃ dagdhapāṣāṇacūrṇaṃ mastake dattvā vastramṛttikayā sarvāṃ kumpāṃ muktvādho manaḥśilāṃ prati praharadvādaśakaṃ yāvat haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The very best kaṇayarī realgar is to be ground in a mortar and put into a jar. Having covered the mouth of the jar with mica, and having placed powdered burnt stone mixed with salt on the top, and having sealed the whole jar with cloth and clay, a violent fire is to be kindled below, toward the realgar, for twelve praharas.

children.text: tataḥ sattvamuḍḍīya kaṇṭhe lagati kumbhodaraṃ ca riktaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then the essence flies up and adheres to the neck, and the belly of the jar becomes empty.

children.text: evaṃ kumpaṃ bhaṅktvā kaṇṭhalagnaṃ sattvaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, after breaking the jar, the essence stuck to the neck is to be taken.
Thus the procedure for extracting the essence of śilā (realgar).
Now, the making of the liquefaction of the six metals in three forms is as follows.

children.text: svabhāvena mṛtasya bhekasyodaraṃ vidārya sphāṭikojjvalaṭaṅkaṇakṣārasyātisūkṣmāḥ khoṭāṃs tatra kṣiptvā tato ghṛtatailādinā digdhvā madhye sthāli bhekaṃ muktvopari pradhvarāṃ ḍhaṅkaṇīyaṃ dattvā bhūmimadhye sthālī nikhanyate ||
children.translated_text: Having split open the belly of a frog that has died naturally, one should put into it very fine pieces of crystalline, bright borax alkali. Then, after smearing it with ghee, oil, and the like, one places the frog in the middle of a pot, puts a sloping lid over it, and buries the pot in the ground.

children.text: ṣaṣṭidinaiḥ punaḥ sthālīmākṛṣya madhyātsarvaṃ gṛhītvā kharale piṣṭvā cūrṇaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: After sixty days, one should pull out the pot again, take everything from inside it, grind it in a mortar, and make a powder.

children.text: tataḥ sarvottamaṃ suvarṇagadyāṇakaṃ gālayitvā vallamātraṃ bhekacūrṇaṃ madhye kṣipyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, after melting a gadyāṇa of the very best gold, one puts into it a valla-measure of the frog powder.

children.text: tatas tat suvarṇaṃ punarbandhaṃ nāpnoti kiṃtu dravameva tiṣṭhati ||
children.translated_text: Then that gold does not become solid again, but remains liquid.
This, in this way, is the liquefaction of gold.

children.text: iyaṃ ca suvarṇadrutirevaṃ kāntalohe rūpye vaṅge nāge tāmre ca gadyāṇamātre ca gālite vallamātraṃ bhekacūrṇaṃ kṣipyate ||
children.translated_text: And this same gold-liquefaction is used with kāntaloha, silver, tin, lead, and copper: when a gadyāṇa-measure of each has been melted, a valla-measure of frog powder is added.

children.text: tato dravarūpāṇi sarvāṇi bhaveyus tattannāmnī ca drutir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then all of them become liquid in form, and the liquefaction bears the name of each respective metal.
Thus, lohadruti, rūpyadruti, vaṅgadruti, nāgadruti, and tāmradruti.
Thus the first making of the liquefaction of the six metals.

children.text: pañcāṅgapītadevadālīkhaṇḍāni kṛtvā karpare jvālayitvā gāḍhaṃ bhasma kriyate tatastasyā eva devadālyā rasena bhāvanā tasya bhasmano dātavyā ||
children.translated_text: Having cut up the five parts of yellow devadālī and burned them in a potsherd, one makes a dense ash. Then that ash is to be given a trituration with the juice of that same devadālī.

children.text: tataḥ pañcadaśavarṇikakāñcanagadyāṇakaṃ gālayitvā vallamātraṃ devadālībhasma kṣiptvā jāraṇīyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, after melting a fifteen-varṇika gadyāṇa of gold, one should add a valla-measure of devadālī ash and digest it.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥpunarvallamātrakṣepe yadā gadyāṇakamātraṃ bhasma jīrṇaṃ syāttadā kāñcanadrutir bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by repeated additions of a valla-measure, when a gadyāṇa-measure of ash has been digested, there is gold-liquefaction.
In the same way, with iron and the other metals too, by digestion with devadālī ash there is the liquefaction bearing each respective name.
Thus the second making of the liquefaction of the six metals.

children.text: śvetadevadālipañcāṅgakhaṇḍāni kṛtvā karpare jvālayitvā bhasma kṛtvaikaviṃśatibhāvanāṃ gomūtreṇa bhasmano dattvā pūrvavat ṣaḍlohamadhye śvetadevadālībhasma lepyam ||
children.translated_text: Having cut up the five parts of white devadālī, burned them in a potsherd, and made ash, one should give the ash twenty-one triturations with cow urine; as before, white-devadālī ash is to be smeared among the six metals.
There is liquefaction of all the metals.
Thus the third making of the liquefaction of the six metals.
In this way there are three varieties of making metal-liquefaction.

children.text: manaḥśilayā nāgaṃ haritālena vaṅgaṃ hiṅgulena lohaṃ śuddhagandhakena tāmraṃ tilamākṣikeṇa rūpyaṃ nāgena suvarṇaṃ ca mriyate ||
children.translated_text: Lead is killed by realgar, tin by orpiment, iron by cinnabar, copper by purified sulfur, silver by tilamākṣika, and gold by lead.
Then, “by whatever procedure,” and so on.

children.text: tāmrasya pattraṃ vā cūrṇaṃ kṛtvā tatastāmraṃ dviguṇaṃ śuddhaṃ gandhakacūrṇaṃ kumārīrase nāgo dugdhena vā gāḍhaṃ mṛditvā pūpādvayaṃ ca kṛtvā madhye pūrvakṛtatāmrapattracūrṇaṃ vā kṣiptvā pūpādvayaṃ śarāvasampuṭe muktvā saṃdhau vastramṛttikayā liptvā sarvato mṛttikayā liptvā kaṭāhamadhye śarāvasampuṭe kṣiptvā chāṇakaiśca kaṭāhaṃ bhṛtvā nirjvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having made copper into leaf or powder, then grinding purified sulfur powder twice the quantity of that copper firmly in kumārī juice, or lead with milk, and making two cakes, one should place the previously prepared copper leaf or powder between the two cakes. Having put the two cakes in a covered pair of earthen bowls, smeared the joint with cloth and clay, coated it all around with clay, placed the covered bowls inside a cauldron, and filled the cauldron with cow-dung cakes, it is to be fired until burnt out.

children.text: tato jvalitvā śītale jāte sati tāmraṃ mṛtaṃ grāhyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, when it has burned and become cool, the killed copper is to be taken.
Thus the procedure for killing copper.

children.text: yena vidhinā gandhakenātra tāmraṃ māritaṃ tenaiva vidhinā nāgādīni pañca lohāni kārye sati māraṇīyāni ||
children.translated_text: By the same procedure by which copper has here been killed with sulfur, the five metals beginning with lead are to be killed when there is need.
Thus the procedure for killing the six metals.

children.text: bījapūrasya vṛntam utpāṭya madhye utkīrya randhraṃ kṛtvā tatra hīrakaṃ jātyaṃ kṣiptvopari vṛntenācchādya vastramṛttikayā samagraṃ bījapūrakaṃ veṣṭayitvā tato hastamātraṃ dīrghā hastamātraṃ pṛthulā hastamātraṃ cādha evaṃ gartāṃ kṛtvā sthāpitaiḥ chāṇakaiḥ pūrayitvā tatra bījapūrakaṃ muktvopari mukhe karparaṃ dattvā chāṇakeṣu vahnir deyaḥ
children.translated_text: Having pulled out the stalk of a bījapūra citron, hollowed out the middle, and made a cavity, one should put a genuine diamond there, cover it above with the stalk, wrap the whole citron with cloth and clay, then make a pit one hasta long, one hasta broad, and one hasta deep, fill it with arranged cow-dung cakes, place the citron there, put a potsherd over the mouth above, and set fire to the cow-dung cakes.

children.text: tato jvalitvā śītalībhūte vīḍāpūrvaṃ tataḥ punardvitīyaṃ bījapūramānīya pūrvavatsarvaṃ kṛtvā gartāyāṃ hīrakabījapūre kṣiptvā chāṇakāni jvālayitvā śītalībhūte sati bījapūramadhyāddhīrako grāhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when it has burned and become cool, after the previous vīḍā, one should again bring a second citron fruit, do everything as before, put the diamond into the citron fruit in the pit, kindle the cow-dung cakes, and, when it has become cool, take the diamond from the middle of the citron fruit.

children.text: evaṃ navanavavāraṃ navanavair bījapūraiḥ sa eva hīrakaḥ pacanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: In this way, nine times, with ever-new citron fruits, that same diamond is to be cooked.

children.text: tato vaḍavāikānisāhāyāṃ vartayitvā tat piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā tatra madhye sa eva hīrakaḥ kṣepyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, having rolled it in vaḍavāikānisāhā, made that into a lump, that same diamond is to be placed in its middle.

children.text: tatastaṃ piṇḍaṃ śarāvasampuṭāntaḥ kṣiptvā sarvato vastramṛttikayā liptvā pūrvataḥ kṛtagartāṃ chāṇakaiḥ bhṛtvā tasyāṃ gartāyāṃ śarāvasampuṭaṃ madhye muktvāgnir jvālanīyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then that lump should be put inside a covered pair of earthen dishes, plastered all around with cloth and clay; the previously made pit should be filled with cow-dung cakes, the dish-cover placed in the middle of that pit, and the fire kindled.

children.text: tataḥ śītalībhūte punaranyāsāṃ vaḍavāikānāṃ piṇḍamadhye tameva hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā tathaiva jvālayitvā hīrako grāhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, when it has become cool, the very same diamond should again be put into the middle of a lump of other vaḍavāikās, burned in the same way, and taken out.

children.text: evaṃ navavāraṃ navanavābhir vaḍavāikābhiḥ sa eva pacanīyaḥ rājabadaryāḥ kisalayarūpāṃ komalāṃ śākhāmānīya tasyāṃ chidraṃ kṛtvā nesahiṅguṃ tatrādha ūrdhvaṃ ca dattvā chidramadhye tameva hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā vastramṛttikayā nicchādya pūrvaṃ chāṇakapūrṇagartāyāṃ pacet ||
children.translated_text: In this way, nine times, with ever-new vaḍavāikās, that same diamond is to be cooked. Having brought a tender shoot in the form of a sprout of royal jujube, making a hole in it, placing nesahiṅgu below and above, putting that same diamond in the middle of the hole, covering it with cloth and clay, one should cook it in the former pit filled with cow-dung cakes.
