children.text: tataḥ punarbadarīśākhākisalayacchidre hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā tathaiva gartāyāṃ pacanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again the diamond is to be placed in a hole in a sprouting branch of jujube and cooked in the pit in just the same way.

children.text: evaṃ navavāraṃ navanavo rājabadarīśākhākisalayaiḥ sa eva hīrakaḥ pacanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, nine times, with ever-new sprouting branches of royal jujube, that same diamond is to be cooked.

children.text: tato mahato nesahiṅgukhoṭasya madhye randhraṃ kṛtvā tameva hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ ca nesahiṅgunā ācchādyopari māṣapīṭhīṃ dadyāt tatastailapūrṇe pātre taṃ hiṅgukhoṭaṃ kṣiptvādho 'gnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made a cavity in the middle of a large lump of nesahiṅgu, one should place that same diamond in it, cover the opening with nesahiṅgu, put black-gram paste over it, and then, after placing that lump of asafoetida in a vessel filled with oil, kindle the fire beneath.
Then again, in a fresh lump of hiṅgu, the same procedure is to be done.

children.text: evaṃ navavāraṃ navanavair nesahiṅgukhoṭaiḥ sa eva hīrakaḥ pacanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, nine times, with ever-new lumps of nesahiṅgu, that same diamond is to be cooked.

children.text: thūthāviḍena taṃ hīrakaṃ sampiṣya pūrvokte rase śanaiḥ śanairjāraṇīyo hīrakaḥ
children.translated_text: Having ground that diamond with thūthāviḍa, the diamond is to be digested gradually and gently in the previously mentioned <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Thus ends the first procedure for the digestion of annapathya diamond.

children.text: mahiṣīṇāṃ karṇamalān gṛhītvā jātyān hīrān veṣṭayitvā tair malaistato malaveṣṭitāṃstān sūraṇakṣudrakandeṣu chidrāṇi kṛtvā tatra ca kṣiptvā sarvataḥ karpaṭamṛttikayā liptvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭo dātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having taken the ear-wax of buffalo cows and wrapped genuine diamonds with that wax, one should then make holes in small tubers of elephant-foot yam, put those wax-wrapped diamonds there, plaster them all around with cloth and clay, and give a kurkuṭapuṭa firing in the ground.

children.text: tataḥ punar hīrakaṃ gṛhītvā tathaiva mahiṣīkarṇamalair veṣṭayitvā sūraṇakṣudrakandamadhye kṣiptvā vastramṛttikayā sarvato liptvā bhūmau chāṇakaiḥ kurkuṭapuṭo deyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again, taking the diamond, wrapping it in the same way with buffalo ear-wax, putting it in the middle of a small tuber of elephant-foot yam, plastering it all around with cloth and clay, a kurkuṭapuṭa firing with cow-dung cakes should be given in the ground.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punarekaviṃśativārān mahiṣīkarṇamalena veṣṭayitvā sūraṇakṣudrakaṃ teṣu ca kṣiptvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭān dattvānnapathyahīrakāḥ sādhanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, again and again for twenty-one times, after wrapping annapathya diamonds with buffalo ear-wax, putting them into small elephant-foot-yam tubers, and giving kurkuṭapuṭa firings in the ground, they are to be prepared.
Thus ends the second procedure for making diamonds annapathya.

children.text: yā bhūmyā mardakī bhūmiphoḍī tasyāḥ pattrāṇi komalāni vartayitvā piṇḍīṃ ca kṛtvā madhye jātyahīrakān kṣiptvā golakān kṛtvā tān śarāvasampuṭamadhye muktvā saṃdhau karpaṭamṛttikāṃ ca dattvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭaṃ dātavyam ||
children.translated_text: Of the plant called mardakī of the earth, bhūmiphoḍī, having rolled its tender leaves and made a lump, one should put genuine diamonds in the middle, make balls, place them in a covered pair of earthen dishes, apply cloth and clay at the joint, and give a kurkuṭapuṭa firing in the ground.

children.text: tataḥ punastathaiva bhūmyāmardakīpiṇḍīmadhye hīrān kṣiptvā golakān kṛtvā śarāvasampuṭe ca kṣiptvā karpaṭamṛttikāṃ ca saṃdhau dattvā bhūmau kurkuṭapuṭo deyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then again, in the same way, after placing the diamonds in the middle of a lump of bhūmyāmardakī, making balls, placing them in a covered earthen dish, and applying cloth and clay at the joint, a kurkuṭapuṭa firing should be given in the ground.

children.text: evaṃ navanavair bhūmyāmardakīpattrapiṇḍīgolakaiste hīrakā bhūmau catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ kurkuṭapuṭāni dattvānnapathāḥ kāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, with ever-new balls made from lumps of bhūmyāmardakī leaves, those diamonds are to be made annapatha by giving sixty-four kurkuṭapuṭa firings in the ground.
This is the meaning.
They become cooked like food, and they are digested in <s>rasa</s> (mercury).
Thus ends the third procedure for making diamonds annapatha.

children.text: ayaṃ hīrako'gninā na dahyate ghanairāhato na bhajyate pānīye na bruḍati ataḥ kāraṇāt hīrakaḥ parīkṣituṃ duḥśakyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This diamond is not burned by fire, is not broken when struck with hammers, and does not sink in water; for this reason a diamond is difficult to test.
Nevertheless, the test is stated.

children.text: prathamaṃ hastayor hīrakaṃ kṣiptvā tato viṃśatihīrakān hastayormuktvā hastābhyāṃ te hīrakā mardanīyās teṣāṃ ca madhye ye hīrakāstejorahitā na syustathā yeṣu rekhā ekāpi na bhavati te jātyā hīrakāḥ ||
children.translated_text: First, having placed a diamond in the hands, and then placing twenty diamonds in the hands, those diamonds should be rubbed with the hands. Among them, those diamonds which do not lose their brilliance and in which there is not even a single line are genuine diamonds.
The rest are not genuine.

children.text: tataśca pakvakarparam ānīya tatrānekān kaḍukān kṛtvā teṣu hīrakān kṣiptvā taṃ hīrakaṃ karparaṃ līhālaṅkair dhmātvāgnivarṇaṃ kṛtvā samabhāgamelitanaramūtrathoharadugdhābhyāṃ vidhmāpyo hīrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then one should bring a fired potsherd, make many little hollows in it, place diamonds in them, blow that potsherd containing the diamonds with līhālaṅkas until it has the color of fire, and quench the diamond with human urine and thohara milk mixed in equal parts.

children.text: evaṃ navanavaiḥ karparaiḥ saptavāraṃ hīrakāḥ pacanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, with ever-new potsherds, the diamonds are to be cooked seven times.
Then, in the first turn here, the diamonds remain just as they were.
In the second turn they become loṣula; in the third turn they are without brilliance.

children.text: caturthavāre vartulāḥ pañcamavāre kartaryā chinnāḥ chidyante ||
children.translated_text: In the fourth turn they are round; in the fifth turn, cut with scissors, they are cut apart.
In the sixth turn they break when rubbed by the hand.

children.text: saptamavāre bhasmarūpāstataśca tadbhasma kumpe kṣiptvā mocyam ||
children.translated_text: In the seventh turn they become ash; then that ash should be put into a kumpe and released.
Thus ends the first calcination of diamond into ash.
The sulfur is āmalasāraka.
Orpiment, realgar, and golden pyrite are to be used.

children.text: etān caturo'pi samabhāgena melayitvā jalena sampiṣya rābasadṛśān kṛtvā tataḥ puṣpāvalyā bahūni puṣpāṇi nisāhāyāṃ vartayitvā piṇḍaṃ ca kṛtvā tanmadhye hīrakān kṣiptvā golākārapiṇḍaṃ ca vidhāya vajramūṣāmadhye taṃ golakaṃ kṣiptvāgnivarṇaṃ ca dhmātvā pūrvakṛtarābamadhye punaḥ punaḥ kṣiptvā mūṣāṃ vidhmāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having mixed these four also in equal parts, ground them with water, and made them like rāba, then, after rolling many flowers of puṣpāvalī with nisāhā and making a lump, one should put the diamonds in its middle, form a spherical lump, place that ball inside a diamond-crucible, blow it until it has the color of fire, and again and again plunge it into the previously prepared rāba, causing the crucible to be quenched.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi tān hīrakān tathā khāparapiṇḍamadhye kṣiptvā vajramūṣāmadhye kṣiptvā dhmātvā ca rābāmadhye vidhāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then again, after putting those diamonds in just the same way into the middle of a potsherd lump, placing it in a diamond-crucible, blowing it, and quenching it in the rāba, one should cool it.

children.text: evaṃ navanavauṣadhaiś caturdaśavārān hīrakānpacet tataḥ sukhena vajrāṇi bhasmībhavanti tacca bhasma kumpe kṣepyam ||
children.translated_text: In this way one should cook the diamonds fourteen times with ever-new medicines; then the diamonds easily become ash, and that ash should be put into a kumpe.
Thus ends the second calcination of diamond into ash.

children.text: ketakīnāṃ stanānnisāhāyāṃ jalaṃ vinaiva gāḍhaṃ vartayitvā vastreṇa ca gālitvā raso grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From the stalks of ketakī, after rolling them firmly with nisāhā without any water and filtering them through cloth, the juice is to be taken.

children.text: tatastena rasena manaḥśilāṃ vartayitvā tayā hīrakān saṃveṣṭya vajramūṣāmadhye kṣiptvāgninā tāṃ vajramūṣāṃ dhmātvāgnivarṇaṃ kṛtvārkadugdhena vidhyāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having rolled realgar with that juice and wrapped the diamonds with it, one should put them inside a diamond-crucible, blow that diamond-crucible with fire until it has the color of fire, and quench it with arka milk.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi ketakīstanarasavartitamanaḥśilayā vajrāṇi veṣṭayitvā vajramūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā dhmātvā cārkadugdhena vidhyāpayet evaṃ punaḥpunaḥ saptavelaṃ kṛte vajrāṇi bhasmībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Then again, after wrapping the diamonds with realgar rolled in ketakī-stalk juice, placing them in a diamond-crucible, blowing them, and quenching them with arka milk, when this has been done seven times again and again, the diamonds become ash.
Thus ends the third calcination of diamond into ash.

children.text: iha śveta ākamadāramūlāni jvālayitvā līhālakāḥ kāryāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, after burning the roots of white ākamadāra, līhālakas are to be made.

children.text: tatasteṣu lihālakeṣu yatnena gartakān kṛtvā teṣu gartakeṣu vajrāṇi prakṣipya suvarṇasambandhini agniṣṭe kṣiptvā āmbilī āulibabūla ||
children.translated_text: Then, after carefully making little pits in those līhālakas, putting diamonds in those pits, and placing them in a fire-brick connected with gold, āmbilī, āuli, and babūla are used.

children.text: līhālakair agnisamānaṃ dhmātvā kulathyāḥ kvāthamadhye kṣiptvā vidhyāpayet anayā yuktyā hīrakāḥ sukhenāpi bhasmībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: After blowing with līhālakas until it is like fire, one should throw it into a decoction of horse gram and quench it. By this method diamonds easily become ash.
Thus ends the fourth calcination of diamond into ash.

children.text: ihāmukhā ulyāmūlāni tvaksaṃyuktānyeva samānīya teṣāṃ śrīkhaṇḍaśeṣādha kṣiptvā sā mūṣāgniṣṭake muktvāgninā dhmātvā thoharadugdhe ḍhālanīyā ||
children.translated_text: Here, having brought ulyā roots together with their bark, placing the remainder of sandalwood among them, putting it in a crucible on a fire-brick, and blowing it with fire, it should be poured into thohara milk.
By this method diamonds are easily killed.

children.text: teṣāṃ ca mṛtānāṃ bhasma kumpe kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: And the ash of those killed diamonds should be put into a kumpe.

children.text: anena hīrakabhasmanā yatkarma yaśca prabhāvaḥ so 'gre bhaṇiṣyate ||
children.translated_text: The operation and effect belonging to this diamond ash will be stated later.
Thus ends the fifth making of diamond ash.
In this way the calcination of diamond into ash is accomplished by five varieties.
Thus ends the procedure for diamond.
Now the purification of sulfur.

children.text: sthālikāmadhye dugdhaṃ kṣiptvā mukhe śaithilyadātharaṃ baddhvā tatra dāthare gandhakaṃ kṣiptvā kaṇṭhe mṛttikayā liptvopari agniṣṭaṃ kṣiptvā ghaṭīdvayaṃ yāvajjvālayet ||
children.translated_text: Having put milk inside a cooking pot, tied a loose dāthara over the mouth, placed sulfur there on that dāthara, smeared the neck with clay, placed fire-bricks above, one should burn it for two ghaṭīs.

children.text: tato gandhako galitvā yo dugdhamadhye yāti sa śuddhagandhako jñeyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the sulfur that melts and goes into the milk is to be known as purified sulfur.
Thus ends the first purification of sulfur.
Now the second purification of sulfur.

children.text: karṣaṃ vā kuḍachī vā ghṛtenābhyajya tatastatra gandhakaṃ kṣiptvādho 'gnir jvālanīyaḥ tāvad yāvad gandhakas tailopamāno bhavati tatas tadgandhakatailaṃ dugdhamadhye ḍhālyate tato dugdhaṃ na gṛhyate ||
children.translated_text: After smearing either a karṣa vessel or a kuḍachī with ghee, one should put sulfur there and kindle fire below until the sulfur becomes like oil. Then that sulfur-oil is poured into milk, but the milk is not taken.
This itself is purified sulfur.

children.text: eva ca prakāradvayena yo gandhakaḥ śodhito bhavati ||
children.translated_text: And thus the sulfur that has been purified by the two methods
is used in operations with <s>rasa</s> (mercury), and no other.
Thus it is easy to understand.
Thus ends the second purification of sulfur.
Thus, easily understood. Next, the gandhaka-pīṭhā.

children.text: tāmrapātraṃ prathamaṃ nimbukānāṃ rasaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ prakṣālyātyujjvalaṃ ca kṛtvā sarvaśuddharasasya rantī tathā śuddhagandhakarantī ca prakṣipyāṅgulyā gāḍhaṃ pramardya gandhakasūtapīṭhī kāryā ||
children.translated_text: First, after repeatedly washing a copper vessel with the juices of lemons and making it very bright, one should put in a rantī of wholly purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and likewise a rantī of purified sulfur, and rub them firmly with a finger; a sulfur-mercury pīṭhī is to be made.
Thus ends the first gandhaka-pīṭhī.

children.text: amalasārasya gandhakasya gadyāṇāḥ 20 tathā śuddhasūtasya gadyāṇāḥ 20 ekatra kharale mardayitvā sūkṣmāṃ kajjalīṃ kṛtvā vastreṇa gālayitvā tato hemavallyā gadyāṇaṃ kandānāṃ śrīkhaṇḍena vā rasena vā gāḍhaṃ sampiṣya pīṭhī kāryā evaṃ ca prakāradvayena gandhapīṭhī niṣpadyate ||
children.translated_text: After grinding together twenty gadyāṇas of āmalasāra sulfur and twenty gadyāṇas of purified mercury in a mortar, making a fine kajjalī, and filtering it through cloth, one should then grind it firmly with a gadyāṇa of hemavallī tubers, or with sandalwood or its juice, and make a pīṭhī. Thus by these two methods gandha-pīṭhī is produced.

children.text: tataḥ pātālagaruḍasya pattrāṇi vartayitvā pīṭhīṃ kṛtvā tanmadhye gandhakapīṭhīṃ kṣiptvā golakaṃ ca kṛtvā taṃ golakaṃ śarāvasampuṭe kṣiptvā saṃdhau karpaṭamṛttikāṃ dattvā jvaladbhiraṅgāraiḥ kukkuṭapuṭaṃ dattvā svabhāvaśītalaṃ gandhakapīṭhīcūrṇaṃ kumpe kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after rolling the leaves of pātālagaruḍa and making a pīṭhī, putting the gandhaka-pīṭhī into its middle and making a ball, one should place that ball in a covered pair of earthen dishes, apply cloth and clay at the joint, give a kukkuṭapuṭa firing with burning coals, and, when naturally cooled, put the gandhaka-pīṭhī powder into a kumpe.

children.text: tataścatuḥṣaṣṭigadyāṇakena rūpyasya gālayitvā madhye eko gandhakapīṭhīcūrṇaṃ gadyāṇakaṃ kṣipyate pañcadaśavarṇikaṃ hema bhavatyeveti ||
children.translated_text: Then, after melting sixty-four gadyāṇas of silver, one gadyāṇa of gandhaka-pīṭhī powder is added into the middle; it indeed becomes fifteen-varṇika gold.
Thus, through the instruction of the guru, other operations that make gold also succeed.

children.text: iti gandhakapīṭhī dvitīyā tathā karmāṇi ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second gandhaka-pīṭhī, and also the operations.
Now, gandhaka oil.

children.text: sarvottamasājīmaṇacatuṣkasya cūrṇaṃ sthālyāṃ kṣiptvā saṃdhyāyāṃ jalaghaṭastatra kṣepyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having put the powder of four maṇas of the very best sājī into a pot, at evening a water-jar is to be placed there.

children.text: tataḥ prātaḥ sājījalaṃ nītāryakābasaṃtyaktvā grāhyam tathā sarvottamapāṣāṇamaṇacatuṣkacūrṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ tathā gandhakāmalasārasya maṇaikaṃ cūrṇaṃ sūkṣmamubhayaṃ piṣṭvā ekatra ca gāḍhaṃ piṣṭvā sthālyāṃ kṣiptvā tataḥ prathamagṛhītaṃ sarjikājalamanyasyāṃ sthālyāṃ muktvālpaghaṭamānamupari kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Then in the morning the sājī-water should be drawn off, rejecting the kābasa, and taken. Likewise, fine powder of four maṇas of the very best stone, and also one maṇa of fine powder of gandhaka-āmalasāra: after grinding both, and grinding them together firmly in one place, one should put them into a pot. Then, having put the sarjikā-water first obtained into another pot, one should pour over it the measure of a small jar.

children.text: evaṃ ca kṛte gandhakasya tailameraṇḍītailavad uparyāgacchati tataśca tailaṃ śītalībhūtaṃ satkumpake kṣepyam ||
children.translated_text: When this has been done, the oil of gandhaka comes up like castor oil; then, when the oil has become cool, it is to be put into a good kumpaka vessel.
Thus ends gandhaka oil.

children.text: iha śuddharasasya gadyāṇān daśa tathā gaṃdhakatailagadyāṇakaṃ ca bhūdharayantre vinyasya mukhe koḍīyakaṃ dattvā saṃdhau vastramṛttikayā liptvā caturbhiḥ chāṇakaiḥ puṭaṃ dātavyam ||
children.translated_text: Here, ten gadyāṇas of purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury), together with one gadyāṇaka of gandhaka oil, should be placed in a bhūdhara apparatus; after putting a koḍīyaka at the mouth and smearing the joint with cloth and clay, a puṭa firing with four cow-dung cakes is to be given.

children.text: tataḥ punarapi teṣveva sūtasya daśagadyāṇakeṣu gandhakatailagadyāṇakaṃ muktvā bhūdharayantre vinyasya mukhe koḍīyakaṃ dattvā vastraṃ mṛttikayā sandhau liptvā caturbhiḥ chāṇakairbhūmau kukkuṭapuṭaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: Then again, into those same ten gadyāṇakas of <s>sūta</s> (mercury), one should put a gadyāṇaka of gandhaka oil, place it in the bhūdhara apparatus, put a koḍīyaka at the mouth, smear the cloth with clay at the joint, and give a kukkuṭapuṭa firing in the ground with four cow-dung cakes.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ karaṇena yadi sūtena daśaguṇaṃ gandhakatailaṃ jīrṇaṃ bhavati tadā pūrvoktāyā hemarājerdaśa vallān sūtamadhye kṣiptvā bhūdharayantre vinyasya koḍīyakasaṃdhau vastramṛttikāṃ ca dattvā caturbhiśchāṇakaiḥ pūrvavatpuṭaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: By doing this again and again, if the <s>sūta</s> (mercury) digests ten times its amount of gandhaka oil, then ten vallas of the previously described hemarāji are to be placed in the middle of the <s>sūta</s>; after placing it in the bhūdhara apparatus and applying cloth and clay to the koḍīyaka-joint, a puṭa is to be given as before with four cow-dung cakes.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaḥ paṭacatuṣṭayadānena hemarājeḥ karṣe jīrṇe sati sa sūtaḥ saṃgrāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by repeatedly giving four layers of cloth, when a karṣa of hemarāji has been digested, that <s>sūta</s> is to be collected.

children.text: tataḥ śuddhatārasya patrāṇi tena dravarūpeṇa tena liptvā sarāvasaṃpuṭe tāni patrāṇi muktvā sandhau karpaṭamṛdaṃ dattvā bhūmau chāṇakaiḥ kukkuṭapuṭaṃ dīyate pañcadaśavarṇaṃ hema bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then leaves of purified <s>tāra</s> (silver), smeared with that in liquid form, should be placed in a covered pair of earthen bowls; after applying rag-clay at the joint, a kukkuṭapuṭa firing is given in the ground with cow-dung cakes. It becomes gold of fifteen-varṇa quality.
Thus ends the first making of gold.

children.text: rūpyasya bhāgā dvādaśa tāmrasya bhāgāḥ ṣoḍaśa evamaṣṭaviṃśatibhāgān vajramūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvā gālayitvā ca candrārkanāmā ṣoṭaḥ kāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Twelve parts of silver and sixteen parts of copper, thus twenty-eight parts, should be put into a diamond crucible, melted, and made into a lump called candrārka.

children.text: tatastasya ṣoṭasya patrāṇyekāṃgulapramāṇāni kārayitvā sarāvasaṃpuṭe muktvā sandhau vastramṛdaṃ dattvā bhūmau chāṇakaiḥ kukkuṭapuṭaṃ dīyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, after making leaves of that lump one finger in measure, placing them in a covered pair of earthen bowls, and applying cloth-clay at the joint, a kukkuṭapuṭa firing is given in the ground with cow-dung cakes.
By the second procedure, gold of fifteen-varṇa quality is produced.

children.text: tathā pittalapatrāṇi pūrvoktayuktyā jīrṇahemarājisūtena liptvā tathaiva kukkuṭapuṭe datte pañcadaśavarṇikaṃ hema bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, when brass leaves are smeared by the previously stated method with <s>sūta</s> that has digested hemarāji, and are given in the same way in a kukkuṭapuṭa firing, gold of fifteen-varṇa quality is produced.
Thus by three procedures there is the production of gold with gandhaka oil.
Thus ends the operations with gandhaka oil.

children.text: iha prathamaṃ varttulākārāṃ mūṣāṃ kṛtvopari gostanākāraṃ nālaṃ ca kṛtvā vajramūṣā vidheyā ||
children.translated_text: Here first, having made a round crucible, and having made above it a tube shaped like a cow's udder, one should prepare a diamond crucible.

children.text: tato yena sūtena pūrvoktayuktyā daśaguṇaṃ gandhakatailaṃ jīrṇaṃ tato hemarājikarṣaśca jīrṇaṃ taṃ rasaṃ vajramūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvopari kaṅguṇītailaṃ tathā kṣipedyathā sa pārado bruḍati ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>rasa</s> by which, according to the method stated before, ten times the amount of gandhaka oil has been digested and a karṣa of hemarāji has also been digested, should be put into the diamond crucible; above it one should pour kaṅguṇī oil in such a way that the mercury sinks.

children.text: tataḥ sā mūṣāgniṣṭake muktvā iṅgālair dhmātavyā ||
children.translated_text: Then that crucible should be placed on a fire-brick and blown with coals.

children.text: tathā yāvanmātraḥ mūṣāyāmasti tāvanmātrāṃ hemarājiṃ mūṣāyāṃ gālayitvā vajramūṣāstharasamadhye kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, as much hemarāji as there is in the crucible should be melted in a crucible and poured into the <s>rasa</s> standing in the diamond crucible.

children.text: tataḥ sahasravedhī ṣoṭo bhavati sa ca saṃgrāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then it becomes a thousandfold-penetrating lump, and it should be collected.

children.text: tathā tārasya tāmrasyādiśabdādvaṅgasya ca gadyāṇasahasrakaṃ pṛthak pṛthak mūṣāyāṃ gālayitvā sahasravedhitasyaikaiko gadyāṇakaḥ pṛthak pṛthak sarvaṣoṭamadhye kṣipyate sarvāṇi tārādīni pṛthak hema bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, a thousand gadyāṇas each of silver, copper, and, by the word 'and so on,' tin, should be melted separately in crucibles; one gadyāṇaka of the thousandfold-penetrating material is put separately into the midst of each entire lump, and all the metals beginning with silver separately become gold.
Thus ends the second transformation procedure using gandhaka oil.
Now, gandhaka water.

children.text: sarvottamasājimaṇaniṣadrasūkṣmacūrṇīkṛtya sandhyāyāṃ maṇamekaṃ sājikumbha eko jalamiti sthālyāṃ kṣiptvā prātaḥ kāvasasaṃtyatkvānītāryajalaṃ grahītvā sājīmarṇe kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having made fine powder of the very best sājī, of a maṇa and a niṣadra, at evening one should put into a pot one maṇa of sājī and one water-jar of water; in the morning, after rejecting the kāvasa and drawing off the water, one should take it and pour it onto the sājī-measure.

children.text: eva ṣaḍbhirdinaiḥ ṣaṇmaṇān kṣiptvā nīvāsarjikājale atisvacchaṃ kṛtvā āmalasārakagandhakastena jalena piṣṭvā vārisadṛśaḥ kṛtvā kumbhe kṣiptvā karpaṭamṛttirāveṣṭya mukhe 'bhrakacātikāṃ dattvā patraculhake pracchanno 'gnirahorātraṃ jvalati tatra culūkakupaṃ nikṣipya paritaḥ ṣaḍaṃgulapramāṇā rakṣā deyā sacakumkas tatra nikṣiptaḥ satnekaviśatidināni sthāpayitvā karṣaṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In this way, over six days, after adding six maṇas and making it very clear in the nīva-sarjikā water, āmalasāraka-gandhaka is to be ground with that water, made like water, put into a jar, wrapped with rag-clay, and given a mica saucer at the mouth. When a covered fire burns day and night on a leaf-stove, a culūka-cup is set down there, protection measuring six aṅgulas is given all around, and, with its cakumka placed there, it should be kept for twenty-one days and then drawn out.

children.text: tāvatā ca kālena gandhakaḥ kumpamadhyaṃ sājīkṣāreṇa saha bhrāmyan pītatoyo nālikerajalasadṛśo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In that much time, the gandhaka, moving together with the sājī-alkali inside the kumpa vessel, becomes yellow water, like coconut water.

children.text: idaṃ ca gandhakavāri hṛtipīṭhīti nāmnā vārttikendramadhye vikhyātaṃ jñātavyam ||
children.translated_text: And this sulfur-water should be known as famous in the center of the vārttika under the name hṛtipīṭhī.

children.text: śodhitapāradasya catvāro vallāḥ gandhakavāriṇā ghaṭīdvayaṃ yadi kṣipyante tadā bhasmībhavanti ||
children.translated_text: If four vallā-measures of purified mercury are put for two ghaṭīs into sulfur-water, then they become ash.

children.text: tataḥ śuddharūpyasya patrāṇi tena bhasmanā liptvā vajramūṣāyāṃ tāni patrāṇi vaṅkalidhamanyā gāḍhaṃ dhmātvā gālayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having smeared leaves of purified silver with that ash, one should place those leaves in a vajra-crucible and melt them, blowing strongly with a vaṅkalidhamanī bellows.
Then the silver becomes black.

children.text: tato'sya kṛṣṇarūpyasya gadyāṇāḥ 8 sarvottamanavakahemagadyāṇāḥ 12 ubhayaṃ viṃśatigadyāṇakā gālyante pañcadaśavarṇikaṃ hema bhavati ||
children.translated_text: After that, eight gadyāṇas of this black silver and twelve gadyāṇas of the very best nine-fold gold, both together making twenty gadyāṇas, are melted; it becomes fifteen-varṇika gold.

children.text: tathā śuddharasaṃ karpare kṣiptvādho mṛdvagniṃ jvālayet ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, having put purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury) in a potsherd, one should kindle a gentle fire below.
Above, one should add sulfur-water drop by drop.

children.text: evamekaviṃśatidināni nirantaraṃ gandhakavāriṇā siktaḥ susūto niṣpadyate baddhaḥ ṣoṭaśca bhavati ||
children.translated_text: In this way, when good mercury has been sprinkled continuously with sulfur-water for twenty-one days, it is produced bound, and also becomes a ṣoṭa pellet.

children.text: tataḥ pātālagaruḍasya patrāṇi vartayitvā tataḥ piṇḍīṃ kṛtvā piṇḍimadhye ṣoṭaṃ ca kṣiptvā bhūmau kukkuṭasaṃjñaṃ puṭaṃ deyam ||
children.translated_text: Then, having rolled leaves of pātālagaruḍa and made a lump from them, one should put the ṣoṭa in the middle of the lump and give a firing called kukkuṭa in the ground.

children.text: paraṃ nirdhūmairjvaladbhiraṃgārais tathā ca kṛte sa ṣoṭaḥ pīto bhavati tataḥ śuddharūpyasya catuḥṣaṣṭigadyāṇān gālayitvā ṣoṭagadyāṇako madhye kṣipyate sarvottamaṃ hema bhavati yata eṣā gandhakadrutipīṭhī catuḥṣaṣṭipravedhikā vartate ||
children.translated_text: But this is to be done with smokeless, blazing coals; and when it has been done thus, that ṣoṭa becomes yellow. Then, after melting sixty-four gadyāṇas of purified silver, the one-gadyāṇa ṣoṭa is put into the middle, and it becomes the best gold, since this gandhakadruti-pīṭhī has a sixty-fourfold penetrating power.
Thus the operations of gandhakadruti-pīṭhī.
Now the purification of tālaka.

children.text: godaṃtī haritālāyāstāvatpatrāṇi kāryāṇi yāvatpunardvidhā na bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Leaves of godantī-haritāla should be made so thin that they do not split again into two.

children.text: tatastāni patrāṇi pāṣāṇacūrṇasyāchibhṛtāyāṃ sthālyāṃ dolāyaṃtre ca tāpayitvādho haṭhāgninā praharadvayena svedanīyāni ||
children.translated_text: Then those leaves, placed in a pot filled with fine stone powder, should be heated in a swing apparatus and sweated below with intense fire for two praharas.

children.text: tata uttārya jalena kṣālayitvā ātape śoṣayitvā luṇayuktakāṃjikapūrṇasthālyāṃ dolāyantre ca tāpayitvā haṭhāgninā praharadvayena svedanīyāni ||
children.translated_text: Then, having taken them out, washed them with water, dried them in the sun, placed them in a pot full of sour gruel mixed with salt, and heated them in a swing apparatus, they should be sweated with intense fire for two praharas.

children.text: punaruttārya jalena prakṣālya gavādidugdhena pūrṇasthālyāṃ svedayetpraharadvayam ||
children.translated_text: Again, having taken them out and washed them with water, one should sweat them for two praharas in a pot filled with milk from cows and other animals.

children.text: tato jalena prakṣālyātape śoṣayitvā kuṣmāṇḍaphalaṃ khaṇḍaśaḥ kṛtvā tadrasena pūrvavatpraharadvayaṃ svedanīyāni ||
children.translated_text: Then, having washed them with water and dried them in the sun, one should cut a kuṣmāṇḍa fruit into pieces and sweat them as before for two praharas in its juice.

children.text: tataḥ payasā prakṣālyātape śoṣayitvā vaḍavāīkā nisāhāyāṃ vartayitvā tadrasena yāmadvayaṃ pūrvavat svedyāni evaṃ pañcabhiḥ śodhanaiḥ śuddhaharitālā nirviṣībhavati ||
children.translated_text: Then, having washed them with milk and dried them in the sun, one should roll them in vaḍavāikā-nisāhā and sweat them as before in its juice for two yāmas. Thus, by five purifications, purified haritāla becomes free of poison.

children.text: yāvacca sā na śodhyate tāvatsā dattā satī hṛdayasya kledaṃ dhūrmaṃ recaṃ tāpaṃ nāḍisaṃkocam antardāhaṃ ca karoti ||
children.translated_text: And so long as it is not purified, when administered it causes moisture in the heart, smoke-like obstruction, purging, heat, contraction of the channels, and internal burning.

children.text: ataḥ pūrvaṃ sā śodhitā amṛtasamānā bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, when it has first been purified, it becomes like nectar.
Thus the rule for purifying godantī-haritāla.
Now the operations with purified tālaka.

children.text: śuddhasūtasya gadyāṇāḥ 4 śuddhatālasya gadyāṇāḥ 20 evaṃ caturviṃśatigadyāṇān khalve prakṣipya tathā chālīvasāyāḥ palikārdhaṃ ca prakṣipyaikaṃ dinaṃ piṣṭvā tatsarvaṃ kuṃpake kṣiptvā mukhe karparacātikāṃ dattvā ākaṇṭhaṃ saptabhiḥ karpaṭamṛttikābhiḥ kumpakamāveṣṭya saṃkīrṇāmuccāṃ ca culhīṃ kṛtvopari kumpako yathā dolāyantro dṛśyate tathā moktavyo'dhaśca praharamekaṃ prathamamṛduvahnijvālanīyastato haṭhāgniḥ ||
children.translated_text: Four gadyāṇas of purified mercury and twenty gadyāṇas of purified tāla, thus twenty-four gadyāṇas, should be put into a mortar; half a pala of chālī-vasā should also be added, and the mixture ground for one day. Having put all that into a kuṃpaka flask, placed a potsherd cap at the mouth, wrapped the flask up to the neck with seven layers of cloth and clay, made a narrow and high stove, and set the flask above so that it appears like a swing apparatus, one should first kindle a gentle fire below for one prahara, and then an intense fire.

children.text: tāvatā ca tālakasatvaṃ proḍḍīya kumpakaṃṭhe lagati ||
children.translated_text: By that much, the essence of tālaka flies up and adheres to the neck of the flask.

children.text: tataḥ kumbhaṃ tyaktvā kaṃṭhakāttatsarvamādāya kharale kṣiptvā chālīvasāpalikārdhena dinamekaṃ mṛditvā dvitīye kuṃpake kṣiptvā saptabhirvastramṛttikābhir liptvā saṃkīrṇoccaculhikāyām āropya pūrvavadadho'gnirjvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having discarded the pot, taken all that from the neck, put it in a mortar, and rubbed it for one day with half a pala of chālī-vasā, one should put it into a second kuṃpaka, smear it with seven layers of cloth and clay, place it on a narrow high stove, and kindle the fire below as before.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ chālīvasāpalikārdhena kharale piṣṭvā tṛtīyakuṃpake pūrvavatsaṃkīrṇācca culhikāyāṃ sarvaṃ kāryaṃ tato yadi saptabhiḥ kuṃpakaiḥ saptavāramevaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ tad bhavati tadā kālikā kaṃṭhake yāti kuṃpabundhe ca jalasadṛśā yekaṇās tiṣṭhanti te tālakasatvarūpāḥ kālikavarjitā grāhyāḥ tatastaṃ tālakasatvaṃ tolayitvā tasmāddviguṇaṃ śuddhapāradaṃ cobhayaṃ kharale kṣiptvā niṃbukarasena mṛditvā sutaptālakasaṃbhavā pīṭhī kāryā mardane ca niṃbukarasaḥ punaḥ punaḥ kṣepyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, again grinding it in the mortar with half a pala of chālī-vasā and putting it in a third kuṃpaka, everything should be done as before in the narrow stove. Then, if it has been processed seven times in seven kuṃpakas, the black matter goes to the neck, while in the bottom of the kuṃpa there remain particles like water; these, in the form of tālaka-essence and free from blackness, are to be taken. Then, after weighing that tālaka-essence, one should put twice as much purified mercury together with it into a mortar, rub it with lemon juice, and make a pīṭhī produced from well-heated tālaka; during the rubbing lemon juice should be added again and again.

children.text: tatastāṃ pīṭhīṃ vastre baddhvā lavaṇayuktakāṃjikapūrṇasthālikāyāṃ niṃbukakhaṇḍāni prakṣipya dolāyaṃtreṇa dinamekaṃ svedayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having tied that pīṭhī in cloth, one should put pieces of lemon into a pot filled with salty sour gruel and sweat it for one day by means of a swing apparatus.

children.text: lavaṇakāṃjikaṃ ca naṣṭaṃ naṣṭaṃ muhurmuhuḥ kṣepyaṃ tataḥ svedottīrṇāṃ tāṃ pīṭhīmātape saṃśoṣya tattulyaṃ ṭaṃkaṇakṣāram ||
children.translated_text: And as the salty sour gruel is used up again and again, it should be added repeatedly. Then, after taking that pīṭhī out from the sweating, drying it thoroughly in the sun, one should add an equal amount of ṭaṅkaṇa alkali.

children.text: tāṃ ca pīṭhīṃ piṣṭvā tato mīṇapūpādvayaṃ kṛtvaikasyāṃ pūpāyāṃ pīṭhīṃ kṣiptvā dvitīyāṃ copari dattvā veḍhinikāṃ kṛtvā tato yāvanmātrā sā pīṭhī tāvanmātraṃ śuddharūpyaṃ vajramūṣāyāṃ gālayitvopari veḍhanī kṣipyate ||
children.translated_text: And having ground that paste, then making two wax cakes, placing the paste in one cake and putting the second on top, one should make a wrapping. Then, after melting in a diamond-crucible an amount of purified silver equal to that paste, the wrapping is thrown on top.
Then, when it is strongly blown from below, the wax, borax, and alkali are burned away.
The orpiment becomes a lump of silver.

children.text: tataḥ śuddhatāmrasya catuḥṣaṣṭigadyāṇakān gālayitvā ekakhoṭagadyāṇo madhye kṣipyate sarvottamaṃ rūpyaṃ bhavati
children.translated_text: Then, after melting sixty-four gadyāṇakas of purified copper, one gadyāṇa of the lump is thrown into the middle; it becomes the best silver.
This should be known as the sixty-fourfold penetration of the orpiment-silver lump.

children.text: tathā pratidinaṃ prabhāte utthāya yo ratimātraṃ ṣoṭaṃ kurute tasya ṣaḍbhiḥ māsairaṣṭādaśakuṣṭhāni praṇaśyanti ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, one who rises every day at dawn and prepares a rati-measure of <s>ṣoṭa</s>, for him the eighteen forms of kuṣṭha disappear in six months.

children.text: navā dantā udgacchanti keśāḥ kṛṣṇā bhavanti palitāni yānti valināśaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: New teeth grow, the hair becomes black, gray hairs go away, and wrinkles are destroyed.
Thus the operations with orpiment.
Now, the threefold liquefaction of abhraka.

children.text: vyāghramadanākhyakodravānāṃ setikāṃ piṣṭvā tanmadhyānmāṇakadvayaṃ susūkṣmacūrṇamādāya sthālyāṃ kṣiptvopari kāṃjikaṃ tathā jalaṃ cākaṇṭhaṃ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Having ground the setikā of the grains called vyāghramadana, one should take from it two māṇakas of very fine powder, put it in a cooking pot, and pour over it sour gruel and also water up to the neck.

children.text: tacca saptabhirdinair atyamlaṃ bhavati tathānena vidhinā śeṣamāṇadvayenātyartham amlaṃ jalaṃ kṛtvā ekaśaḥ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: In seven days that becomes extremely sour; in the same way, with the remaining two māṇakas, very sour water should be made and used one by one.

children.text: tataḥ śvetābhrakamaṇacūrṇaṃ tenāmlajalena saholūkhale yāmamekaṃ kuṭṭayitvā tasminneva jale dināni rāhayitvā paścādātape śoṣayitvā tato rālāṭaṃkaṇakṣārau lavaṇaṃ kaṇagugguluśceti caturṇāmauṣadhānāṃ pratyekamaṇacaturthāṃśaṃ tathā tilasya gadyāṇān 20 guḍasya gadyāṇān 20 vallapīṭhīpālī 1 madhukarṣaḥ 1 dugdhakarṣaḥ 1 etatsarvamekatra kṛtvā dhānyābhrakeṇa saha muhurmuhuḥ kṣodayitvā gadyāṇakadaśakamātrāḥ anekapūpāḥ kṛtvā rākṣase yantre 'ṅgārān kṣiptvā ekāṃ pūpāṃ muñcet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having pounded powder of white abhraka-gem with that sour water in a mortar for one yāma, kept it in that very water for some days, and afterwards dried it in the sun, one should add rāla, borax, alkali, salt, and kaṇa-guggulu, a quarter māṇa of each of these four drugs, also twenty gadyāṇas of sesame, twenty gadyāṇas of jaggery, one pālī of valla paste, one karṣa of honey, and one karṣa of milk. Having put all this together and repeatedly crushed it with dhānyābhraka, one should make many cakes of about ten gadyāṇakas each; then, having put coals in a rākṣasa apparatus, one should release one cake.
And when one has melted, one should throw in a second.
In this way all of them are to be melted within one prahara.

children.text: tataḥ svayaṃ śītalāḥ pūpāḥ samuddhṛtya tāsāṃ madhyād dhānyābhrakasaṃbhavā drutirgrāhyā ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the cakes have cooled by themselves, they should be taken out, and from their middle the liquefaction produced from dhānyābhraka is to be collected.
By this method the liquefaction of dhānyābhraka occurs easily.
Thus the first making of dhānyābhraka-liquefaction.

children.text: śvetadhānyābhrakacūrṇaṃ gadyāṇadvayamadhye dugdhapālī 1 kṣiptvā sehulakaḥ pātyate ||
children.translated_text: Into two gadyāṇas of white dhānyābhraka powder, one pālī of milk is put, and a sehulaka is fed.
And that sehulaka is placed inside a chamber.

children.text: yathānyatra na yāti tataḥ punaḥ śvetadhānyābhrakagadyāṇadvayaṃ madhyakṣiptaṃ dugdhaṃ pāyyate evaṃ bahubhir dinaiḥ punaḥ punastasya pāne sehulakena yatpurīṣaṃ muktaṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ tolayitvā caturthabhāgena madhye ṭaṅkakṣāraṃ kṣiptvā ghṛtamadhubhyāṃ piṣṭvā lepasadṛśaṃ kṛtvā tena lepena pūrvakathitatumbīnalayaṃtramūlaṃ liptvā līhālakair vaṅkanālīdhamaṇyā so'dhomukhaṃ kumpako yaṃtro dhmātavyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: So that it does not go elsewhere, then again two gadyāṇas of white dhānyābhraka are placed in the middle and milk is made to be drunk. Thus, over many days, by repeatedly giving it drink, all the excrement released by the sehulaka is weighed; one fourth part of borax-alkali is put into it, it is ground with ghee and honey, and made like a paste. With that paste the base of the previously described tumbī-nala apparatus is smeared, and that downward-facing kumpaka apparatus is to be blown with līhālakas through a curved tube-blower.
Then that paste becomes a liquefied form.
Thus the second transformation, the liquefaction of dhānyābhraka.

children.text: svecchayā mṛtaḥ śaśako bhramadbhiryadi dṛśyate tadā tasya mastakamadhyānmecakaṃ gṛhītvā dhānyābhrakasya gadyāṇān 40 gāḍhaṃ peṣayitvā tanmadhyān mecakamātraṃ cūrṇaṃ mecakamadhye kṣiptvā dvayaṃ mṛditvā piṇḍaṃ ca kṛtvā ghṛtena tailena vā liptasthālikāmadhye taṃ piṇḍaṃ kṣiptvā upari pradhvarāṃ ḍhaṃkaṇīṃ dattvā pārśveṣu sarvatra vastramṛttikābhir niśchidrīkṛtya sā sthālī kaṇakoṣṭamadhye kṣiptvā 21 dināni sthāpyā tāvatā ca mecakamadhye ye kṛmayo jāyante te'bhrakaṃ bhakṣayitvā paścādbubhukṣayā tāpena ca mriyante ||
children.translated_text: If, while wandering, one sees a hare that has died of its own accord, then one should take the black substance from the middle of its head, grind forty gadyāṇas of dhānyābhraka thoroughly, put from that powder an amount equal to the black substance into the black substance, knead the two, and make a lump. Having put that lump in a pot smeared with ghee or oil, placed a sloping lid above, sealed all around the sides without gaps with cloth and clay, that pot is to be put inside a grain chamber and kept for twenty-one days. By that time, the worms that arise in the black substance eat the abhraka and afterwards die from hunger and heat.

children.text: tatasteṣu kṛmiṣu mṛteṣu yattatra śeṣaṃ muhurati sā dhānyābhrakadrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, when those worms have died, what remains there as a repeatedly melted residue is the dhānyābhraka-liquefaction.
Thus the third transformation, the liquefaction of dhānyābhraka.
In making the liquefaction of abhraka, these alone are the three varieties.
Now their operations will be stated.

children.text: śuddharasasya daśa gadyāṇān vajramūṣāmadhye prakṣipya tāṃ mūṣāṃ vālukāyantre caṭāyya dinamekaṃ mṛdvagniṃ jvālayet ||
children.translated_text: Having placed ten gadyāṇas of purified <s>rasa</s> (mercury) inside a diamond-crucible, one should set that crucible on a sand-bath apparatus and kindle a gentle fire for one day.

children.text: upari bhūnāgasatvasya binduṃ binduṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: Above it one should repeatedly add, drop by drop, the essence of bhūnāga.
Then a mouth of the mercury is produced.
Everything that is given is digested.

children.text: tato nisāhāmatisūkṣmāṃ cilhāṃ prapiṣya vastreṇa niścotya raso grāhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having very finely ground nisāhā and cilhā, squeezed them through a cloth, the mercury is to be taken.

children.text: tato yasmiñjale palaṃ māti tāvanmātraṃ kāntapātramākaṇṭhaṃ pūrayitvā kāntapātraṃ vālukāyantre caṭāyitvādho mṛduragniḥ punaḥ punarahorātraṃ jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having filled a magnetic vessel up to the neck with as much water as measures one pala, one should set the magnetic vessel on a sand-bath apparatus, and a gentle fire below is to be kindled again and again for a day and night.
Then, through the union of abhraka-liquefaction and mercury, or else, an abhra-ṣoṭa is produced.

children.text: tatastaṃ ṣoṭaṃ vajramūṣāyāṃ prakṣipya gadyāṇān 20 madhye prakṣipya gāḍhaṃ gālayitvā samuttārayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, after placing that <s>ṣoṭa</s> pellet in a diamond crucible, putting it among twenty gadyāṇas, melting it thoroughly, one should take it out.
Then a gadyāṇa that is imperishable, stainless, and brilliant is produced.
It becomes silver of the very best kind.

children.text: asau vaṃge śatamadhye vedhako rasaḥ tathā yaḥ sadā prabhāte ratimātraṃ ṣoṭaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: This <s>rasa</s> has penetrating power in a hundred parts of tin; and he who always in the morning takes a rati-measure of <s>ṣoṭa</s>
within six months becomes one whose body is undecaying and free from disease. Thus are the threefold operations of mica-liquefaction.
Now, <s>bhūnāga</s>.

children.text: pañcadaśavarṇikaṃ suvarṇagadyāṇān caturo gālayitvā jarakīśadalavat kaṇṭakavedhyāni patrāṇi kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: Having melted four gold gadyāṇas of fifteen-varṇa quality, one should make leaves like leaves of jarakīśa, pierceable by thorns.

children.text: tato narakapālaṃ tathā dhattūrakamūlaṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak ghṛṣṭvā samabhāgena ekīkṛtya pūrvasādhitahīrakabhasmano gadyāṇa ekastanmadhye kṣepyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then human skull and dhattūra root, ground separately, should be combined in equal portions; one gadyāṇa of the previously prepared diamond ash is to be put into that mixture.

children.text: tataḥ kharale kṣiptvā sarvaṃ tāvatpeṣayet yāvadaikātmyaṃ prāpnoti tatastena hemapatrāṇi liptvā aṃdhamūṣāyāṃ kṣiptvopari bhūnāgasatvagadyāṇaṃ ca muktvā prathamaṃ koṣṭhikāyāṃ līhālakairbhṛtvā vakranālīdhamaṇyā dhamet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having put everything in a mortar, one should grind it until it becomes homogeneous. Next, having smeared the gold leaves with it and placed them in a sealed crucible, and having put above them a gadyāṇa of <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s> (essence of bhūnāga), one should first fill it in a furnace with līhālaka coals and blow it with a bent-tube bellows.
Then one should blow it on a fire-brick with līhālaka coals.
Then one should blow it in a pit with līhālaka coals.

children.text: evaṃ trivelaṃ dhmātaḥ sannasau hemavajrabhasmabhūnāgasattvajaḥ ṣoṭo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: When it has thus been blown three times, this becomes a <s>ṣoṭa</s> pellet produced from gold, diamond ash, and <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>.

children.text: tatastaṃ ṣoṭaṃ mardayitvā sūkṣmaṃ cūrṇaṃ kāryam ||
children.translated_text: Then that <s>ṣoṭa</s> should be rubbed and made into a fine powder.

children.text: tataḥ kācakumpīmākaṇṭhaṃ saptabhiḥ karpaṭamṛttikābhir āveṣṭya prathamaṃ karṣamātraṃ bhūnāgasatvaṃ tathā śuddhapāradasya ṣaḍ gadyāṇakāṃśca prakṣipya vālukāyantre tāṃ kumpīmāropyādho haṭhāgnir jvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then a glass flask should be wrapped up to the neck with seven layers of rag-clay; first a karṣa-measure of <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s> and six gadyāṇakas of purified mercury should be put in, the flask set on a sand apparatus, and a fierce fire kindled below.
When the <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s> has disappeared, it should be added again.

children.text: kiṃ bahunā saptadināni nirantaraṃ kumpikābhūnāgasattvena bhṛtaiva dhāraṇīyā ||
children.translated_text: In short, for seven days without interruption the flask must be kept filled with <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>.

children.text: yathā ṣaṭpañcāśadbhiḥ praharaiḥ śuddhasūtaṣaḍgadīyāṇakā gāḍhaṃ vighate ||
children.translated_text: In this way, over fifty-six praharas, the six gadyāṇakas of purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) thoroughly break down.

children.text: tatastasya mukhaṃ jāyate sa ca sūto rākṣasanāma jāyate sarvabhakṣaka ityarthaḥ tataḥ pūrvaṃ yo hemavajrabhūnāgasatvaṣoṭo vartayitvā cūrṇito'sti tanmadhyāccatuḥṣaṣṭitamaṃ bhāgaṃ gṛhītvā kharale rākṣasasūtamadhye kṣiptvā piṣṭvā piṣṭvā jāraṇīyaḥ tataḥ punaścatuḥṣaṣṭitamo bhāgastatra piṣṭvā jāraṇīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then an opening appears in it, and that <s>sūta</s> becomes named Rākṣasa, meaning 'eater of everything.' Then from the previously made and powdered <s>ṣoṭa</s> of gold, diamond, and <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>, one should take a sixty-fourth part, put it in a mortar into the Rākṣasa mercury, and make it digest it by grinding and grinding; then again a sixty-fourth part is to be ground there and digested.

children.text: evaṃ punaḥ punaścatuḥṣaṣṭitamaṣoṭabhāgajāraṇena ṣaḍ gadyāṇāḥ ṣoṭasya jāraṇīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by repeatedly digesting sixty-fourth parts of the <s>ṣoṭa</s>, six gadyāṇas of <s>ṣoṭa</s> are to be digested.

children.text: tato rākṣasasūtaṣaḍgadīyāṇamadhye śodhitotkṛṣṭapāradagadīyāṇān ṣaṭ melayitvā te dvādaśagadīyāṇā mūṣāyāṃ prakṣipya gālanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, into the six gadyāṇas of Rākṣasa mercury, six gadyāṇas of purified excellent mercury should be mixed; those twelve gadyāṇas are to be put in a crucible and melted.
It becomes a <s>ṣoṭa</s> with hundredfold penetrating power.

children.text: tato rūpyasya tāmrasya nāgasya vā gadīyāṇakaśataṃ gālayitvā ṣoṭagadīyāṇāḥ kṣipyate ||
children.translated_text: Then, after melting a hundred gadyāṇakas of silver, copper, or lead, a gadyāṇa of <s>ṣoṭa</s> is put in.
It becomes gold of fifteen-varṇa quality.
This <s>rasa</s> has hundredfold penetrating power in the three metals.

children.text: tathā prabhāte nityam amṛtakalayā yuktaṃ ṣoṭacūrṇaṃ ratīmātraṃ kurute ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, every morning one takes a rati-measure of <s>ṣoṭa</s> powder joined with amṛtakalā.
For him defects such as wrinkles and grey hair disappear.
And the hairs become black.
Firmness of body arises.
The radiance of the body becomes like gold.

children.text: hemapatrairvajrabhasma nāgasatvena tribhiḥ sādhito'yaṃ ṣoṭo dehakārako lohakārakaśca ||
children.translated_text: This <s>ṣoṭa</s>, prepared with the three substances gold leaves, diamond ash, and lead essence, is body-making and metal-making.
Thus are the operations of gold, diamond ash, and <s>bhūnāga-sattva</s>.

children.text: śrībhairavagaṇādhipatilakṣmīsarasvatībhyo namo'stu yeṣāṃ prasādād guṭikāñjanāni pāradāśca sidhyanti ||
children.translated_text: Homage to glorious <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Gaṇādhipati</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>, by whose favor pills, collyria, and mercuries become perfected.

children.text: tatracaturaśītiḥ 84 guṭikāś caturaśītiḥ 84 aṃjanāni caturaśītiḥ 84 pāradakarmāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Among these there are eighty-four pills, eighty-four collyria, and eighty-four mercury operations.

children.text: evaṃ sarvasaṃkhyayā trayāṇāṃ dvipañcāśadadhikaṃ śatadvayam 252 bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the total reckoning, the three classes amount to two hundred fifty-two.

children.text: eteṣāṃ dvipañcāśadadhikaśatadvayasya madhyādekasya kasyacid guṭikauṣadhasyāñjanasya vā pāradasya vā prārambhe ādau tathāphalaprānte'khaṇḍaṃ tapo vidheyam ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning of any one among these two hundred fifty-two, whether a pill-medicine, a collyrium, or a mercury, and also before the attainment of its result, uninterrupted austerity must be performed.

children.text: tatra prārambhe māsaikādarvāk niṣpattisamaye'pi phalādarvāṅ māsamekaṃ brahmacaryapālanīyaṃ haviṣyānnaṃ paramānnaṃ ca ghṛtādimiśraṃ dugdhaṃ vā bhojanīyam ||
children.translated_text: At the beginning, for one month beforehand, and also at the time of completion, for one month before the result, celibacy is to be observed; one should eat sacrificial food, sweet rice mixed with ghee and the like, or milk.
When the rule of austerity is observed, the procedures succeed.

children.text: yatastapaḥsādhyā rasādayaḥ prayogā ye punaḥ tapohīnāḥ sādhakāste'ntataḥ daivasya karmaṇo doṣam antarāyaṃ vadanti ||
children.translated_text: For operations beginning with <s>rasa</s> are accomplished through austerity; but practitioners who lack austerity finally blame fate, karma, or an obstacle.

children.text: tena tapasvināṃ mukhyena śrīkaṅkālayayoginā vārttoktā dhātuvaṭṭijñaproktā guṭikā vartate ||
children.translated_text: Therefore there is a pill taught in the Vārttā by the foremost among ascetics, the glorious <s>Kaṅkālaya Yogin</s>, and proclaimed by the knower of metal tablets.

children.text: tāsāṃ madhyājjñānaphalāṃ jñānakāraṇaṃ guṭikāṃ vakṣyāmi dvipañcāśadvallamātrauṣadhaniṣpannām ||
children.translated_text: Among them I shall explain the pill whose fruit is knowledge and whose cause is knowledge, prepared from medicines measuring fifty-two vallas.

children.text: tatra catvāro vallā abhrakasatvasya catvāro vallāḥ svarṇamākṣīkasya catvāro vallāḥ śuddharūpyasyaiko vallo hemarājeḥ 7 tathāṣṭādaśasaṃskārairyaḥ pūrvoktaśuddhapāradastasya vallā ekonacatvāriṃśad evaṃ militāḥ sarve dvipañcāśat 52 vallāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There, four vallas of mica essence, four vallas of svarṇamākṣīka, four vallas of purified silver, one valla of hemarāji, and thirty-nine vallas of the purified mercury previously described, purified by the eighteen saṃskāras: thus all together make fifty-two vallas.
Having put them in a mortar, one should grind them for seven days.
Then one should grind the root of the varuṇa tree and śrīkhaṇḍa.

children.text: sarvamauṣadhaṃ vastre baddhvā dolāyantre sthālikāyāṃ tena śrīṣaṇḍena komalavahninā dinadvayaṃ svedayitvottārya guṭikāṃ kṛtvā paścāt krameṇa pañcāmṛtena svedayet ||
children.translated_text: Having tied all the medicine in cloth in a swing apparatus, one should sweat it in a pot with that śrīṣaṇḍa over a gentle fire for two days; after taking it out and making a pill, one should afterwards sweat it successively with the five nectars.

children.text: tatra madhu ghṛtaṃ dadhi dugdhaṃ śarkarā veti pañcāmṛtam ||
children.translated_text: There honey, ghee, curds, milk, and sugar are called the five nectars.
And in that sweating this is the procedure.

children.text: prathamaṃ guṭikāṃ madhunā saha kāṃsyalohapātre vālukāpūrṇasthālikāmadhye kṣepyaḥ 12 sā sthālī culhikāyāṃ caṭāyyādho'ṣṭau praharān vahnirjvālanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: First the pill, together with honey, should be placed in a bronze vessel in the middle of a pot filled with sand; that pot should be set on a stove, and beneath it the fire is to be kept burning for eight praharas.
Honey should be put above.

children.text: tadanu naṣṭe naṣṭe punaḥ punarmadhu kṣepyam evaṃ praharāṣṭakena madhunā svedayitvottārya tato ghṛtena saha kāntalohapātre guṭīṃ prakṣipyāṣṭapraharānsvedayedvālukāyaṃtre ||
children.translated_text: Then, whenever it is exhausted, honey should be added again and again. Thus, after sweating it with honey for eight praharas and taking it out, one should then put the pill together with ghee in an iron vessel and sweat it for eight praharas in the sand apparatus.

children.text: tata evaṃ praharāṣṭakaṃ dadhinā tataḥ praharān 8 dugdhena tataḥ praharān 8 śarkarājalamiti ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, for eight praharas with curds, then for eight praharas with milk, and then for eight praharas with sugar-water.
Thus, after sweating the pill five times with the five nectars,

children.text: tapaḥ kurvato brahmacaryapālayatā hastābhyāṃ pracālya dvipañcāśavallamātrā guṭikā kāryā
children.translated_text: while practicing austerity and observing celibacy, one should roll it with the hands and make a pill measuring fifty-two vallas.
Then, for a woman whose maternal and paternal lineages are pure,

children.text: yā ca brāhmaṇī vā kṣatriyā vā vaiśyī cottamakulaprasūtā ||
children.translated_text: who is a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, or <s>Vaiśyī</s>, and who is born in an excellent family,

children.text: tasyāḥ śūdrīṃ varjayitvā yadā prathamo garbho bhavati tadā māsaikād anantaraṃ sā guṭikā samarpaṇīyā ||
children.translated_text: excluding a <s>Śūdrī</s>, when her first pregnancy occurs, after one month that pill is to be given to her.

children.text: tayā ca bhojanamauṣadhatāmbūlāsvādapānīyapānavelāṃ varjayitvaikaṃ māsaṃ nirantaraṃ mukhe dhāraṇīyā ||
children.translated_text: And she should hold it constantly in her mouth for one month, except at the times of eating food, tasting medicine and betel, and drinking water.

children.text: tato māse gate sati guṭikāyāḥ prabhāvāt pṛṣṭā satī sā strī atītānāgatavartamānaṃ sadyaḥ pratyayakārakaṃ trikālaviṣayajñānaṃ vadati ||
children.translated_text: Then, when the month has passed, by the power of the pill, if questioned, that woman immediately speaks knowledge concerning the three times: past, future, and present, producing direct conviction.
The power of this pill is exceedingly wondrous.

children.text: yato yathā jñānī yadbhāṣate tatsarvaṃ satyaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For whatever a knowledgeable person says becomes wholly true.

children.text: tathā mukhe guṭikākṣepamāhātmyād brāhmaṇī kṣatriyā vaiśyī yāvadvadati tattathaiva bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, through the greatness of placing the pill in the mouth, whatever a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>Kṣatriyā</s>, or <s>Vaiśyī</s> says becomes exactly so.

children.text: yato rasasya pāradasya guṭikānāṃ tathā pātālāñjanādīnām añjanānāṃ prabhāvātiśayo mahān gururityarthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the extraordinary power of <s>rasa</s>, that is, mercury, of pills, and of collyria such as pātālāñjana is very great and weighty; that is the meaning.
This pill is indeed called the vādinī.

children.text: yadyapyasyāḥ samyagāmnāyaḥ sāṃprataṃ nopalabhyate tathāpi kiṃcidakṣarārthaṃ yuktyā kiṃcidguṭikāntarānubhavena kiṃcit tathāvidhaśrutayuktyanusāreṇa vyākhyā ||
children.translated_text: Although a proper tradition for it is not now available, still its explanation is made partly by reasoning from the meaning of the syllables, partly from experience with other pills, and partly according to such traditional reports and reasoning.

children.text: tathā caturaśītiguṭikā 84 caturaśītyaṃjanāni 84 caturaśītirasabhedān 84 parijñāya pūrvaśrīkaṅkālayayoginā nijaśiṣyaparijñānārthaṃ yogakṣemanirvāhārthaṃ sarveṣāmupakārārthaṃ ca kiṃcidrasatattvam upadiṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having understood the eighty-four pills, the eighty-four collyria, and the eighty-four varieties of <s>rasa</s>, the earlier <s>Śrīkaṅkālaya Yogin</s> taught some part of the truth of <s>rasa</s> for the instruction of his own disciples, for the maintenance of welfare and security, and for the benefit of all.

children.text: tatastacchiṣyeṇa svasya visṛtyarthaṃ paraṃ parayāvyavacchedārthaṃ pareṣām upadeśārthaṃ cāyaṃ rasādhyāyo viracitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then this Rasādhyāya was composed by his disciple, for his own forgetting, for preventing the interruption of the succession from one to another, and for instruction of others.
In this treatise there are twenty-one sections.
They are as follows: first, chain-rasa, processed by the eighteen saṃskāras.
Then hemarāji and ghoṣarāji.
Mākṣikarāji.
Nāgarāji.
Second, then the method for extracting the essence of khāpara.
Then the method for extracting the essence of manaḥśilā.
Then the method for calcining the six metals.
Then the threefold production of druti from the six metals.
Then the threefold making of annapatha diamond.
Then the fivefold reduction of diamond to ash.
Then the purification of sulfur in two ways.

children.text: tataḥ dvidhā gandhakapīṭhī tasyāḥ karma ca ||
children.translated_text: Then gandhaka-pīṭhī in two ways and its operation.
Then gandhaka oil.
Then the threefold operation of gold with gandhaka oil.
Then the procedure for the thousandfold-penetrating <s>rasa</s> with gandhaka oil itself.
Then gandhaka-druti-pīṭhī.
Then the operation of gandhaka-druti-pīṭhī.
Then the purification of tālaka.
Then the operation of tālaka.
Then mica-druti in three ways.
Then its operations.
Then the ṣoṭa operations produced from gold, diamond ash, and bhūnāga essence.
Then, indeed, the bālavādanī pill.
Thus the twenty-one sections have been set down.

children.text: te ca yadyapi kiṃcic cānumānasambhavena kiṃcit tathāvidhavārttikendrasaṃsargajātasaṃskāreṇa kiṃcidakṣarārthayuktyā vivṛtya vyākhyātāḥ tathāpi yadi kvāpi kimapyalīkaṃ vyākhyānaṃ bhavet tadā prasadya śrīvārttikendraiḥ śrīrasādhyāyena tadadhiṣṭhātṛdevatābhiśca sarvaṃ kṣantavyam ||
children.translated_text: And although these have been explained by unfolding them, some through the possibility of inference, some through impressions born from association with such venerable <s>Vārttikendra</s>s, and some through reasoning from the literal meaning, nevertheless, if anywhere there should be any false explanation, then, being gracious, all of it should be forgiven by the venerable <s>Vārttikendra</s>s, by the venerable <s>Rasādhyāya</s>, and by the deities presiding over it.
